item.title: Indonesia state utility firm replaces CEO amid widespread power outages
item.description: Indonesian state utility Perusahaan Listrik Negara has replaced its chief executive, the company's commissioner said on Thursday, following a series of power outages across the country in recent months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesian state utility Perusahaan Listrik Negara has replaced its chief executive, the company's commissioner said on Thursday, following a series of [USN:L4N42Q0FD TEXT:"power outages"] across the country in recent months. PLN at a shareholder meeting on Wednesday decided to remove Darmawan Prasodjo and appoint the firm's former risk management director Suroso Isnandar as CEO, its independent commissioner Andi Arief told Reuters Indonesia's power outages have included a major blackout across at least six provinces in Sumatra in May and [USN:L4N4340U8 TEXT:"rolling outages"] in Java and Kalimantan in June and July The latest outage was in Batam on Monday, lasting at least 16 hours Asked if the leadership change was about the blackouts, Andi said no reason was given at the meeting "I suspect this is a routine change, since Darmawan has been in the role for quite a long time," Andi said

item.title: Oil prices fall as investors weigh supply outlook, Middle East tensions
item.description: Oil prices fell more than $1 in early trade on Thursday as investors weighed risks to supply from attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz against US efforts to cut petroleum shipping costs by easing sanctions on vessels.
item.dc:creator: Sam Li, Lewis Jackson
item.content:encoded: Oil prices fell more than $1 in early trade on Thursday as investors weighed risks to supply from attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz against US efforts to cut petroleum shipping costs by easing sanctions on vessels. Brent crude futures fell $1.39, or 1.31%, to $104.67 a barrel by 0116 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down $1.02, or 1.07%, to $94.07, reversing gains from the previous session. WTI rose to a three-week high in the prior session after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran said it was deploying new tactics to target ships in the Strait of Hormuz and keep oil prices high. A container ship and a dry bulk carrier both [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"sank"] near the strait in the past 24 hours after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said on Wednesday. Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. With the Iran war having disrupted shipping and driven up freight costs to record highs, the Trump administration is considering [USN:L1N46017R TEXT:"easing sanctions"] on so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela to help ease prices, a US official said on Wednesday. The new talks centre on the United States potentially allowing "legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said. Increased output from Russia and the Middle East has kept a lid on prices. Russia's crude oil production [USN:L1N46008R TEXT:"rose"] by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million bpd but remained down 870,000 bpd year over year, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday. The IEA also said crude oil exports from Middle East Gulf producers rose by 4.4 million bpd in September to around 75% of prewar levels. In the US, crude oil and distillate inventories fell, while gasoline stocks rose last week, market sources said on Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude stocks [USN:L6N4601BW TEXT:"fell by 11.1 million barrels"] in the week ended October 9, sources said. That was a much bigger draw than analysts [USN:L1N46016I TEXT:"polled"] by Reuters expected. "Despite the sharp inventory draw, oil prices barely reacted. The failure to rise on bullish news suggests investors are cautious about chasing prices higher at current levels," said Haitong Futures in a note on Thursday. Official numbers from the US Energy Information Administration are due at 12 p.m. EDT (1600 GMT), delayed by a day following the Columbus Day holiday on Monday.

item.title: All Blacks make three changes to starting side for second Bledisloe Cup test
item.description: New Zealand coach Dave Rennie has made three changes to his starting side for Saturday's second Bledisloe Cup test against Australia, including bringing in Fabian Holland for Josh Lord at lock and replacing Ethan de Groot with George Bower at loosehead prop.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand coach Dave Rennie has made three changes to his starting side for Saturday's second Bledisloe Cup test against Australia, including bringing in Fabian Holland for Josh Lord at lock and replacing Ethan de Groot with George Bower at loosehead prop. Rennie lost forwards Anton Segner and Asafo Aumua as well as winger Leroy Carter to injuries and concussions sustained in last week's 50-19 victory, which secured the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th consecutive year. Josh Moorby has been promoted from the bench to replace Carter on the left wing but most of the injury-enforced changes are to the bench. Hooker Samisoni Taukei'aho, prop Xavier Numia, loose forward Du'Plessis Kirifi, scrumhalf Cortez Ratima and centre Timoci Tavatavanawai come into the replacements. Richie Mo'unga is once again unavailable because of a calf injury so Damian McKenzie gets another run in the number 10 shirt after a fine game at Eden Park last week. Beauden Barrett again starts at fullback. Forward Ethan Blackadder is also unavailable due to injury. "The Wallabies are a proud side and they'll be hurting after last week," Rennie said in a statement. "It's a great challenge for us to now face them in front of their home crowd in Sydney." New Zealand have beaten Australia in their last 12 meetings. Team: 15-Beauden Barrett, 14-Will Jordan, 13-Quinn Tupaea, 12-Jordie Barrett, 11-Josh Moorby, 10-Damian McKenzie, 9-Cam Roigard, 8-Wallace Sititi, 7-Peter Lakai, 6-Tupou Vaa'i, 5-Fabian Holland, 4-Scott Barrett, 3-Fletcher Newell, 2-Codie Taylor (captain), 1-George Bower. Replacements: 16-Samisoni Taukei'aho, 17-Xavier Numia, 18-Pasilio Tosi, 19-Shannon Frizell, 20-Du'Plessis Kirifi, 21-Cortez Ratima, 22-Timoci Tavatavanawai, 23-Rieko Ioane.

item.title: Brazil's Senate approves shorter workweek in win for Lula
item.description: Brazil's Senate on Wednesday approved a constitutional amendment to reduce the country's workweek from six days to five, providing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva a key legislative win less than two weeks before the country's presidential runoff.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazil's Senate on Wednesday approved a constitutional amendment to reduce the country's workweek from six days to five, providing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva a key legislative win less than two weeks before the country's presidential runoff. The popular labor reform was backed by lawmakers from across Brazil's political spectrum in the two required votes, including by Lula's runoff opponent, right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who had once opposed it. Approved by the Senate after receiving the [USN:L1N4230Q1 TEXT:"green light"] from the lower house in May, the amendment lowers working hours in Latin America's largest economy to 40 hours a week from 44, effectively ending a common practice in some sectors, such as retail, of requiring formal employees to work six days a week. It marks the biggest overhaul of Brazilian labor rights in decades. The government had estimated that the new rules would benefit more than 37 million formal-sector workers, with the new standard to be implemented over a 14-month period. Lula, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, and his government have championed the measure, while Bolsonaro and his Liberal Party long opposed it, arguing the move was designed to boost Lula's reelection prospects. In a post on X, Lula called the amendment a victory for workers. "It's more time to live, rest, be with family, watch your children grow, take care of yourself, and enjoy life," said the president. Bolsonaro, who led Lula in the election's first round vote earlier this month, ultimately [USN:L1N45Z0RL TEXT:"reversed course"] on Tuesday ahead of the Senate vote, saying he would in fact vote to shorten the workweek.

item.title: Nepal, World Bank sign mandate to explore earthquake catastrophe bond
item.description: Nepal and the World Bank have signed a mandate agreement to explore the development of a catastrophe bond that could help the Himalayan nation access funding quickly in case of a major earthquake, the World Bank said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nepal and the World Bank have signed a mandate agreement to explore the development of a catastrophe bond that could help the Himalayan nation access funding quickly in case of a major earthquake, the World Bank said on Thursday. "Under the agreement, the World Bank Group Treasury will work with the Government of Nepal and market participants to assess the feasibility and potential structure of such a transaction," the World Bank said in a statement.

item.title: Norway's wealth fund set to overhaul ethical rules after US scrutiny
item.description: Norway is expected to overhaul the ethical rules for its $2.3 trillion wealth fund in response to the findings of a state-appointed commission due on Thursday, a year after it paused divestments in the face of US scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: Gwladys Fouche
item.content:encoded: Norway is expected to overhaul the ethical rules for its $2.3 trillion wealth fund in response to the findings of a state-appointed commission due on Thursday, a year after it [USN:L1N3WG0KT TEXT:"paused"] divestments in the face of [USN:L6N3UR0DD TEXT:"US"] scrutiny. The Trump administration had [USN:L6N3UR0DD TEXT:"protested"] against the fund's [USN:L8N3UH15F TEXT:"divestment from Caterpillar"] (CAT.N) shares over the use of the US company's bulldozers in Gaza and the occupied West Bank. Weeks later, Norway's parliament [USN:L1N3WG0KT TEXT:"voted in favour of pausing"] ethics-based divestments by the world's largest state-owned fund pending the outcome of a review, the findings of which are due to be released at 0700 GMT on Thursday. The government denied this move was motivated by concerns over consequences of potentially upsetting the US, where more than half of the fund's assets are invested. Before the suspension, the Council on Ethics, the fund's independent ethical watchdog, made recommendations to divest and sent them to the board of the central bank, which had the final say. The board usually followed the council's recommendations. Since the suspension, all recommendations have instead been sent to Norges Bank Investment Management, which is the fund's operator, with no divestments made over the period. Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg said securing the fund, which finances a quarter of the country's public spending, was "one of the most important things we do in Norway". "The world is changing and the value chain is becoming more and more integrated. It is difficult to distinguish between civil and military products," he told Reuters on Wednesday. He also pointed to the concentration of the fund's value in a handful of companies, mostly US tech giants such as Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Apple (AAPL.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) , with 10 accounting for more than 20% of the value of its share portfolio. "This type of concentration ... means that individual decisions can have much greater consequences than in the past," said Stoltenberg, a former NATO secretary-general, adding that his priority was for the fund to remain broadly invested. "We should not do things that can undermine that. At the same time, we must have a good ethical framework," he said in an interview in Norway's parliament. The commission's proposals will form the basis for the government to make its own as part of an annual white paper on the sovereign wealth fund which is expected in spring 2027. DEFENCE COMPANIES One possible change concerns the fund's ban on investing in companies making nuclear weapons, or key components, effectively ruling out the world's largest defence companies. Stoltenberg asked the commission to look at whether nuclear weapons as a deterrent should be taken into consideration. Should the commission recommend lifting this ban, the fund could invest in the largest defence companies. Its exclusion list currently cites Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) , Boeing (BA.N) , Airbus (AIR.PA) , BAE Systems (BAES.L) , Safran (SAF.PA) , Thales (TCFP.PA) , BWX Technologies (BWXT.N) , Northrop Grumman (NOC.N) , Fluor (FLR.N) , General Dynamics (GD.N) , Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII.N) , Jacobs Solutions (J.N) , L3Harris Technologies (LHX.N) and L&T (LART.NS) . Civil society groups, including the Norwegian Red Cross, say that would legitimise investing in weapons of mass destruction. "The way Norway invests significant sums contributes to setting standards globally," the Red Cross said in its submission to the commission. TRANSPARENCY OF THE FUND Stoltenberg [USN:L1N41P0T9 TEXT:"previously told"] Reuters the openness of the fund in publishing the reasons why it was divesting posed dilemmas. Once the fund sold out of a company, the council published its recommendation in full, including its reasoning, based on months or years of investigations, providing a unique source of information for the public and other investors. The idea that these recommendations might no longer be made public has raised concerns among civil society groups, who say doing so provides a key source of information for the general public and investors alike. Some activists are also concerned that the Council on Ethics would be removed altogether.

item.title: Senado aprova fim da escala de trabalho 6x1, em vitória para Lula
item.description: O Senado aprovou nesta quarta-feira a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que extingue a jornada de trabalho conhecida como 6x1 e reduz a jornada de trabalho semanal, em uma grande vitória para o governo Lula num tema que entrou com força na campanha eleitoral, conta com ampla aprovação popular, mas não é bem vista por setores empresariais.
item.dc:creator: Maria Marcello, Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: O Senado aprovou nesta quarta-feira a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que extingue a jornada de trabalho conhecida como 6x1 e reduz a jornada de trabalho semanal, em uma grande vitória para o governo Lula num tema que entrou com força na campanha eleitoral, conta com ampla aprovação popular, mas não é bem vista por setores empresariais. Por uma ampla maioria de votos -- 75 a 1 -- nos dois turnos de votação, senadores aprovaram a PEC, que precisa ser promulgada pelo Congresso para ser efetivamente incorporada pela Constituição. O tema ganhou forte tração durante o período eleitoral. Inicialmente, a proposta de autoria do deputado Reginaldo Lopes (PT-MG) era apoiada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e aliados, que aproveitaram a defesa de sua aprovação como plataforma de campanha, mas não contava com a simpatia do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), que disputa o Planalto com Lula no segundo turno. Flávio e apoiadores acusaram o petista de agir com oportunismo. Em declarações públicas, defenderam uma proposta alternativa, levando em conta uma jornada flexível e a remuneração proporcional à hora trabalhada, em que acordos individuais entre empregados e patrões prevaleçam sobre convenções coletivas. Mas diante da pressão -- pesquisas apontaram neste ano índices próximos de 70% de apoio ao fim da escala 6x1 --, Flávio anunciou na terça-feira que votaria a favor da PEC, alertando, no entanto, que o governo federal terá de pagar uma compensação aos empresários pelo fim do modelo. Aliados do senador chegaram a mencionar, como sugestão, a desoneração da folha de pagamento. Na sessão do Senado de aprovação da PEC, Flávio, que participou remotamente, preferiu não discursar. Logo após a aprovação, Lula afirmou, em publicação no X, que a aprovação da medida configura uma "vitória dos trabalhadores e trabalhadoras". "Hoje é dia de comemorar uma conquista histórica de milhões de trabalhadores e trabalhadoras", disse o presidente no post. A PEC aprovada nesta quarta-feira, dando um fim à escala 6x1, também prevê uma redução de 2 horas semanais na jornada de trabalho -- das atuais 44 para 42 já 60 dias após a promulgação da proposta. A carga horária sofrerá um decréscimo de mais 2 horas um ano após a primeira redução. A proposta estabelece ainda o piso de duas folgas semanais, uma delas preferencialmente no domingo, e garante que não haverá redução de salário.

item.title: Rams' Alaric Jackson has punching suspension cut to 1 game
item.description: Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson had his suspension for punching Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb reduced from two games to one, the NFL announced Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson had his suspension for punching Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb reduced from two games to one, the NFL announced Wednesday. Jackson punched Chubb in the face after the Bills won 37-34 in overtime on Monday night. Chubb said something to Jackson before Jackson walked over in Chubb's direction and delivered the punch. Appeals officer Derrick Brooks, the Hall of Fame linebacker, heard the appeal after being jointly appointed by the NFL and NFL Players Association. Brooks cut Jackson's penalty in half. The NFL previously said Jackson violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship." Jackson, 28, will miss the Rams' home game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. He will be eligible to return to Los Angeles' active roster on Monday, Oct. 19. "Have to make better decisions than that," Rams coach Sean McVay said of Jackson on Tuesday. Chubb, 30, acknowledged the incident after Monday's contest. "It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game, it was a close game," said Chubb, who was pulled away from the confrontation. "They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing, and then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled." --Field Level Media

item.title: Asian markets sell off as AI trades crumble after hot US CPI data
item.description: Markets started the day on the back foot as trading kicked off in Asia on Thursday, as a quicker-than-expected increase in US consumer price inflation upped expectations for the Federal Reserve to act later this year and pushed stocks lower.
item.dc:creator: Gregor Hunter
item.content:encoded: Markets started the day on the back foot as trading kicked off in Asia on Thursday, as a quicker-than-expected increase in [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"US consumer price inflation"] upped expectations for the Federal Reserve to act later this year and pushed stocks lower. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) was down 1.2%, led by a 5.6% plunge in South Korea's KOSPI (.KS11) , while the Nikkei 225 (.N225) fell 1.3%. S&P 500 e-mini futures were down 0.3%. "Asia faces another difficult session," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone Group Ltd in Melbourne. "KOSPI and Nikkei futures point to renewed technology weakness, with leveraged ETF flows and AI infrastructure credit risk firmly in focus." Overnight, [USN:L6N4601BJ TEXT:"stocks on Wall Street"] logged their third day of declines after US consumer price inflation accelerated by more than expected in September. The S&P 500 (.SPX) fell 1.1%, the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) tumbled 1.9% and a gauge of semiconductor stocks (.SOX) extended losses into a sixth day, as the prospect of [USN:L6N4601B1 TEXT:"higher interest rates"] pummelled shares of Oracle, CoreWeave and other AI stocks sensitive to higher borrowing costs. "While the initial selloff was triggered by the hotter-than-expected CPI, tech was the main driver of today’s selloff," JPMorgan analysts wrote in a note. "AI was again the main challenge ... with financing risks and IPO timelines still at the centre of the story." The CPI data lifted expectations of interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve over the course of the year ahead, possibly as soon as later this month. Fed funds futures are now pricing an implied 31.6% probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the US central bank's next two-day meeting on October 28, compared to a 22.1% chance a day earlier, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond fell 4.4 basis points to 5.144%. Against the yen , the US dollar slid 0.2% to 157.925 yen, while the euro was up 0.3% at $1.1194. The Australian dollar declined 0.2% to $0.6956 after employment unexpectedly decreased by 39,300 jobs in September, against expectations of an increase of 20,000. Investor attention turns to speeches from Fed officials speaking in Bangkok, including Chair Kevin Warsh, for clues on the US central bank's next move, as well as US producer prices and retail sales data due for release later on Thursday. AI chip giant TSMC (2330.TW) will also release earnings for the third quarter later in the Asian trading session.

item.title: Australia employment unexpectedly slides in September, jobless at 4.7%
item.description: Australian employment unexpectedly fell in September, data showed on Thursday, while the unemployment rate held at a five-year high, a soft result that had investors paring back wagers on another hike in interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Stella Qiu
item.content:encoded: Australian employment unexpectedly fell in September, data showed on Thursday, while the unemployment rate held at a five-year high, a soft result that had investors paring back wagers on another hike in interest rates. Markets now imply a nearly 90% chance the Reserve Bank of Australia will leave interest rates unchanged at 4.6% in November, up from 66% before the data, after delivering four rate hikes this year. The chance of a move in December has fallen to just 31%, with another rate increase no longer fully priced in. The Australian dollar slipped 0.2% to $0.6956, while three-year government bond futures rallied 11 ticks to 95.19. Figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed net employment slid 39,300 in September from August, when it rose a downwardly revised 29,300. That was the biggest monthly fall since February last year, as part-time roles tumbled 73,700. Analysts had forecast a rise of around 20,000. The jobless rate stayed at 4.7%, with the previous month revised up from an initial 4.6% reading. The participation rate dipped to 66.8%, while hours worked rose 0.1% and underemployment edged up to 6.3%. "The rise in the unemployment rate to 4.7% gives the RBA more room to be patient and assess incoming inflation data before raising rates again," said Oscar Guth, an economist for Oxford Economics Australia. "We expect unemployment to rise further through 2027, exceeding 4.8% late in the year as the lagged effects of oil price shocks and tighter monetary policy continue to affect the labour market." The RBA has warned of caution in interpreting the monthly jobs data given the methodological changes to the survey, arguing that more forward-looking indicators such as job ads pointed to a broadly stable labour market, the minutes of the September policy meeting showed on Tuesday. The central bank has lifted interest rates four times this year to 4.6% to tame inflation, but annual headline inflation ran at 4% in August, and a core measure remained elevated at 3.6%, both above its target band of 2% to 3%.

item.title: Daly, do Fed, diz que devem ser necessários aumentos nos juros, mas não com urgência
item.description: O Federal Reserve provavelmente precisará aumentar ainda mais as taxas de juros de curto prazo para conter a inflação excessivamente alta, afirmou nesta quarta-feira a presidente do Federal Reserve de San Francisco, Mary Daly, mas ela sinalizou que não há necessidade de fazê-lo na reunião do banco central marcada para 27 e 28 de outubro.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: O Federal Reserve provavelmente precisará aumentar ainda mais as taxas de juros de curto prazo para conter a inflação excessivamente alta, afirmou nesta quarta-feira a presidente do Federal Reserve de San Francisco, Mary Daly, mas ela sinalizou que não há necessidade de fazê-lo na reunião do banco central marcada para 27 e 28 de outubro. “É mais provável que precisemos de ajustes adicionais, mas, para mim, o momento certo para esses ajustes ainda está sendo deliberado”, disse Daly à Reuters em entrevista exclusiva. “Não sinto que haja urgência em decidirmos com um conjunto limitado de informações. Acho que temos o tempo de que precisamos.” Vários pares de Daly também sinalizaram nas últimas semanas que é improvável que o Fed aumente as taxas neste mês. A taxa de juros de referência do Fed está na faixa de 3,75% a 4,00%. Os custos dos empréstimos de longo prazo são ainda mais altos, com alguns — como as taxas de hipotecas de 7,5% — freando a demanda em alguns setores da economia. Daly disse que acredita que os mercados financeiros compreendem a “função de reação” do Fed, apontando para a forma como os operadores reagiram aos dados divulgados na manhã desta quarta-feira, que mostraram que a inflação dos preços ao consumidor acelerou para 3,7% nos 12 meses até setembro, um pouco mais forte do que os economistas haviam previsto. O Fed tem como meta uma inflação de 2%, medida por um indicador diferente, mas relacionado. Embora a reação inicial tenha sido “robusta” — os operadores de futuros de taxas rapidamente apostaram em um aumento das taxas pelo Fed em outubro —, os investidores “se acalmaram” após analisar os dados. Os preços mais altos da gasolina impulsionaram o aumento geral, e a inflação subjacente, embora ainda persistente, não apresentou uma alta acentuada. “Definitivamente, esses dados sugerem que o risco para a inflação permanece elevado”, disse Daly. “O risco para a inflação aumentou ainda mais, mas riscos não são realidades, e reagir ao risco quando se tem tempo para tomar uma boa decisão, para mim, parece imprudente.” Daly disse que a estabilidade contínua do mercado de trabalho dá ao Fed margem para se concentrar na estabilidade de preços. Mas, segundo ela, “por que forçar a urgência quando não há necessidade de urgência? Por que não aproveitar o tempo para refletir e deliberar com calma? E ainda temos mais reuniões pela frente.” Os mercados financeiros estão precificando agora cerca de 40% de chance de um segundo aumento consecutivo da taxa de juros pelo Fed na próxima reunião do banco central — uma chance maior do que antes da divulgação dos dados, mas que já não aponta para um aumento como o resultado mais provável, como era o caso logo após a divulgação do relatório de inflação. Os mercados, disse ela, “compreendem que estamos comprometidos com a estabilidade de preços e que faremos o que for necessário para alcançá-la”. Os formuladores de políticas “têm a responsabilidade de se comunicar de forma eficaz com o público e de serem responsáveis, transparentes e claros”, disse ela. “A responsabilidade é ser extremamente claro com as pessoas sobre quais são seus objetivos, pelo que você é responsável e como vai equilibrar os riscos.”

item.title: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia's legal career draws scrutiny
item.description: The new White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia, faced questions on Wednesday about her legal career before becoming the top spokeswoman for US President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Hunnicutt, Karen Sloan, Joe Cash
item.content:encoded: The new White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia, faced questions on Wednesday about her legal career before becoming the top spokeswoman for US President Donald Trump . Zacharia, who joined the White House on Monday, has said she practiced law before entering politics. Trump has described her as an attorney. But Reuters could not find records showing Zacharia was registered as an attorney or member of the bar in any US state or the District of Columbia. The questions about Zacharia's credentials come as she takes the podium just three weeks before November's midterm elections , a critical period when the president is seeking to tout his administration's accomplishments and help his fellow Republicans retain control of Congress. Zacharia was an associate at Zhong Lun Law Firm in Beijing from 2011 to 2013 and general counsel at Fix California, an advocacy group founded by Trump ally Ric Grenell, from 2024 to 2025, according to her LinkedIn profile. In a text message, Grenell said Zacharia was "a senior adviser, who did a lot of different roles," including "leading the outside counsel, who were our lawyers." Zhong Lun did not respond to emailed requests for comment. The White House did not respond to questions about Zacharia's legal background or credentials. "I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials," Zacharia said in an emailed statement on Wednesday. Trump hired Zacharia after expressing concerns about the media coverage of his administration, feeling he needed a new spokesperson who could amplify his achievements, according to two people familiar with the conversations. She replaced [USN:FWN4491F6 TEXT:"Karoline Leavitt"], who left the White House in August. The timing of Zacharia's hiring so close to the midterms caught some White House staff by surprise, one official said. On Tuesday during her first briefing, she took questions from just three reporters before ending the event in under 15 minutes. Her performance was criticized by some media commentators and political analysts, though Trump told reporters: "I thought she was very good." Zacharia earned her law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, according to the university. Nearly all licensed US lawyers first obtain a law degree, but law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar. Asked by a reporter on Tuesday where she had passed the bar exam, Zacharia said, "when I moved to China." In China, the law requires practicing lawyers to be Chinese nationals. Foreign staff can advise and consult on legal matters but not practice law. Renee Knake Jefferson, a University of Houston law professor and legal ethics expert, said the debate over Zacharia’s status is a “fundamental matter of public trust” that goes beyond “professional semantics.” “Of course it goes without saying that one needn’t be a lawyer to serve as the White House press secretary,” Jefferson said. “The public is entitled to accurate information about whether a government official is claiming to hold a professional role that they do not, which is what has been alleged here.”

item.title: US rejects recommendation for ICE body cams to be automatically activated
item.description: The Trump administration has rejected a government watchdog's recommendation that US immigration officials should use technology that would automatically activate body-worn cameras when an officer pulls their weapon or sets off a car siren.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Kristina Cooke
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has rejected a government watchdog's recommendation that US immigration officials should use technology that would automatically activate body-worn cameras when an officer pulls their weapon or sets off a car siren. Automatic activation of body-worn cameras was one of a number of recommendations outlined in a report released on Wednesday by the Government Accountability Office (GAO), an independent nonpartisan watchdog agency for Congress. The recommendation comes as US agencies face mounting scrutiny over enforcement tactics used in an [USN:L4N3SN13Z TEXT:"immigration crackdown"] that has included fatal shootings of two US citizens in Minneapolis, raising questions about officers' accountability. The GAO report said US Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection "should improve body-worn camera program management," adding that CBP and ICE have not updated their program plans since 2022 and 2024, respectively. Covering the period from February 2025 until September this year, the report recommended that ICE implement additional controls to make sure that cameras are activated. "We maintain that additional controls, such as automated camera activation, would provide greater assurance that body-worn cameras meet ICE's desired results for transparency, accountability, and public trust," the GAO said in the report. The Department of Homeland Security, of which ICE is a part, said in comments cited in the report that it did not agree with the recommendation, citing what it said were privacy and operational risks. For ICE, automatic activation risked the possibility of inadvertent or false activations during routine movement, the DHS said in the report. DHS also said in the report that inadvertent or false activations could result in the unauthorized recording of sensitive interactions with informants or victims, or the recording of bystanders engaged in free speech activities in areas where camera use is restricted. ICE has been the face of President Donald Trump's [USN:L6N45D01D TEXT:"deportation drive"], which he says aims to improve domestic security. Rights advocates say the crackdown has violated due process and free speech rights and created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about [USN:L4N3ZU0AN TEXT:"racial profiling"]. Responding to the GAO report's publication, a DHS spokesperson said on Wednesday ICE had acquired devices to equip all officers and agents with body cameras. "Training required to equip individual officers remains ongoing and we expect to complete this training soon," the spokesperson said.

item.title: US considers easing sanctions on shadow fleet vessels to cut freight rates, official says
item.description: The Trump administration is considering easing sanctions on so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Gardner, Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration is considering easing sanctions on so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday. The discussions are happening days after President Donald Trump temporarily [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"lifted sanctions"] on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with a torrent of criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, [USN:S8N43U03J TEXT:"European"] countries and some of Trump's [USN:L1N45Z0TJ TEXT:"fellow Republicans"] in the US Senate. Both Zelenskiy and the US senators called that move a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin that would provide Russia with revenue to keep funding its war in Ukraine. The new talks center on the United States potentially allowing "legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said. That means crude or petroleum products not sanctioned by Washington rather than Russian and Iranian oil, which are under punitive measures. The goal is to get more refined products and crude out of the Gulf, the official said. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in a video to the World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh this week that the administration was talking about easing the sanctions on shadow fleet vessels in an effort to cut record freight rates that have cut into demand for US crude, according to Energy Aspects, a research group. Bits of the talk were broadcast on social media, but Reuters was not able to obtain the full video or a transcript. The Department of Energy said it was not available. Companies seeking to use the sanctioned vessels would have to apply to the US Treasury Department to use the vessels, the official said. The Department of Energy said any move to relieve sanctions on the shadow fleet would not help Russia to move oil or oil products. The Treasury Department referred questions to the Department of Energy. But Trump's push to move Russian diesel to global markets quickly could put pressure on the departments to allow shipment via the vessels. The White House did not respond immediately to a request for comment. High oil and fuel prices are a risk for Trump in the November 3 midterm elections in which Republicans are hoping to maintain control of both chambers of Congress. He lifted the sanctions on Russian diesel through April 7. RECORD HIGHS Tanker freight rates have [USN:L4N45U0OZ TEXT:"soared to record highs"] as the wars in Iran and Ukraine have stoked inflation and put US crude oil out of reach for Asian refiners, pushing them to seek alternatives from the Middle East and Latin America. Energy Aspects said in a note to clients that easing the sanctions on the shadow fleet would not greatly impact freight rates but could allow more movement of oil in the Middle East. Lifting the sanctions on the tankers that are mostly old and not well maintained is "unlikely to add meaningful mainstream fleet capacity overnight, especially as most tankers sanctioned over Russian or Venezuelan links have been actively trading over the past three months," it said in the note. Easing the restrictions "could make a small number of additional tankers available for certain (Strait of) Hormuz shuttle runs," in the waterway between Iran and Oman. Lifting the measures is unlikely to result in a broad easing of freight rates as ship insurers will still be bound by EU and UK regulations, maritime industry sources said.

item.title: Câmara aprova aumento do limite para enquadramento do MEI
item.description: A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta quarta-feira projeto de lei que reajusta o teto para o enquadramento de microempreendedores individuais (MEI), e perdoa dívidas de quase 3,6 milhões de MEIs, além de permitir a contratação de até dois funcionários.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta quarta-feira projeto de lei que reajusta o teto para o enquadramento de microempreendedores individuais (MEI), e perdoa dívidas de quase 3,6 milhões de MEIs, além de permitir a contratação de até dois funcionários. Aprovado por 461 votos a 4, o texto segue para o Senado. O texto eleva o teto de enquadramento do MEI dos R$81 mil de faturamento anual vigentes hoje para R$110 mil, em 2027, e R$140 mil, em 2028. A proposta, apresentada pelo governo em junho, integra pacote anunciado na véspera que também prevê a compra de dívidas privadas desses trabalhadores pela União, repasse direto de recursos para investimento no negócio e dispensa de emissão de notas fiscais. Segundo o ministro do Empreendedorismo, da Microempresa e da Empresa de Pequeno Porte, Paulo Pereira, o projeto vai perdoar R$12,6 bilhões em dívidas tributárias de MEIs. Ao apresentar a proposta em junho, o governo estimou que o impacto fiscal da medida seria de R$1,57 bilhão em 2027, R$3,15 bilhões em 2028 e R$3,38 bilhões em 2029. O pacote anunciado na terça representa o primeiro grande anúncio de medidas após o primeiro turno das eleições e atinge um grupo relevante de pessoas, já que o Brasil tem hoje 17,6 milhões de microempreendedores.

item.title: Trump says he hopes Pope Leo will 'get better fast'
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday he hoped that Pope Leo, who has been diagnosed with lung cancer, would "get better fast."
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday he hoped that Pope Leo , who has been [USN:L1N45Z08S TEXT:"diagnosed"] with lung cancer, would "get better fast." DETAILS AND QUOTES: "I want to see Pope Leo get well," Trump told reporters. "I just want to wish him well, get better fast." Pope Leo, 71, was diagnosed with lung cancer after surgeons removed a part of his right lung on Tuesday, according to the Vatican. His recovery from surgery is [USN:L8N46009K TEXT:"progressing as expected"] and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday. Leo and Trump have been critical of each other in the past. Leo, the first US pope, has called for a "[USN:L8N3WG34Q TEXT:"deep reflection"]" in the US about how migrants are treated under Trump, cast the Trump administration as being "[USN:L8N3WU23M TEXT:"extremely disrespectful"]" to immigrants and criticized what he called their "[USN:L5N3VH1K6 TEXT:"inhuman"] treatment." On the US foreign policy front, the Vatican has [USN:L4N3ZE094 TEXT:"declined to join"] Trump's "Board of Peace" initiative for Gaza and the pope has criticized the US-Israeli war on Iran . Trump called Leo "terrible for Foreign Policy" and "WEAK on Crime" in an online post earlier this year. Late last month, Leo said that concerns about AI having the potential to destroy the world should be taken seriously, in an apparent rebuke of Trump, who has said that fears the technology poses a threat to humanity are a "hoax."

item.title: In Sri Lanka, human-elephant conflict takes deadly toll
item.description: Clad in his khaki wildlife officer’s uniform, Dewagiri Mudiyanselage Thilakaratne Bandara rides his motorbike the short distance from his home to the electric fence that is the main line of defence against the dozens of wild elephants that live in the rapidly shrinking forest nearby.
item.dc:creator: Uditha Jayasinghe, Thilina Kaluthotage
item.content:encoded: Clad in his khaki wildlife officer’s uniform, Dewagiri Mudiyanselage Thilakaratne Bandara rides his motorbike the short distance from his home to the electric fence that is the main line of defence against the dozens of wild elephants that live in the rapidly shrinking forest nearby. The fence stretches 14 km (9 miles) along the Siyambalangamuwa tank, a reservoir in the island's northwest, to protect the more than 2,000 families who live in the nearby villages. Galgamuwa is on the front line of one of the world's most serious human-elephant conflicts. An average of 138 people have been killed in encounters with the animals each year in Sri Lanka since 2019, the second-highest death toll in the world. The death toll for elephants, forced into villages for food as their habitat shrinks, climbed to an average of 402 a year during the same period, the world's highest. “Twenty years ago, we didn’t have this situation because across from the tank there were large forests, but they were eventually cleared and then the elephants started moving closer and that’s how this village started being affected,” Bandara said, as he worked to repair the fence with his team. “When we were little, we had to go to a corner of the tank to see elephants. Now, in the nights, the elephants come to see us.” Sri Lankans have deep cultural ties with elephants. The animals feature in colourful temple pageants, and owning one is a status symbol. Elephants are also a mainstay of the island’s $4 billion tourism industry. But elephant deaths reached a record high of 488 in 2023, according to the Department of Wildlife Conservation (DWC). Data shows dozens were shot as they encroached on villages, while others died from poisoning, electrocution, in train accidents or after falling into wells. 'HE WAS HUNGRY BECAUSE OF US' Bandara, 48, has first-hand experience of how devastating the human-elephant conflict can be. Last December, an elephant wandered into Bandara's backyard to snack on mangoes. He attacked Bandara and his wife, Rathnayake Mudiyanselage Shirani Rathnayake, after she rushed to help him. Bandara was left with a broken leg and dislocated shoulder. Rathnayake, also 48, was trampled and had to have her right leg amputated. She now uses a wheelchair. “Our lives are now completely different from before the elephant attack. My wife and I used to do everything together. We used to farm together. But 200% of those activities have been disrupted. Now we must look after her and the mental strain of that is something we both feel,” Bandara said, standing outside his home. Villagers have been forced to adapt their daily lives to reduce the risk of confrontations. The nearby school starts lessons 30 minutes after the nationally mandated time of 7:30 a.m. to avoid the early morning when elephants might be around. Villagers also finish work earlier so they can get home before dark, while funerals and weddings are scheduled to minimise the chance of an elephant encounter. Bandara and his neighbours have a WhatsApp group dedicated to tracking elephant movements. Neighbours often come together to try and chase away any elephants that attempt a raid, yelling and lighting firecrackers, and also take people to hospital in the event of an attack. Bandara supports ending forest clearing, usually done for farming, and wants to see a commitment to reforestation. Sri Lanka's forest cover has plummeted from roughly 70% in the 1920s to about 34% today, World Bank data shows. To complicate matters, as many as 70% of Sri Lanka’s estimated 7,451 wild elephants live outside protected areas. The elephant population is also growing, recording a 27% increase from a decade ago, according to the latest census data. All this has pushed elephants and people closer. “I do not feel any hatred towards the animal or any animal. He was hungry because of the activities of us humans," Bandara said. "I see this situation more as karma that my wife and I must endure. What will I get by hating that animal? He is innocent." Click on https://reut.rs/4hNnV3S to see the related photo essay

item.title: Law firm Boies Schiller adds white-collar partner in latest DOJ exit
item.description: A US Justice Department official whose work included defending the use of force against allegedly violent protesters during a Chicago immigration crackdown has left to join Boies Schiller Flexner, the law firm said Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: A US Justice Department official whose work included [USN:L6N3WI0WJ TEXT:"defending"] the use of force against allegedly violent protesters during a Chicago immigration crackdown has left to join Boies Schiller Flexner, the law firm said Wednesday. Sarmad Khojasteh, who joined the Justice Department in April 2025 from King & Spalding, will be a partner handling white-collar defense, investigations and commercial litigation in New York and Washington, the firm said. He was most recently deputy assistant attorney general for the Justice Department's special litigation and enforcement and affirmative litigation branches. Boies Schiller cited Khojasteh's work securing a [USN:L6N43317K TEXT:"$600 million settlement"] in July from Chinese technology and e-commerce giant Alibaba (9988.HK) and its US-based payment processor to resolve allegations that they failed to prevent illegal drug sales. "Sarmad brings a deep understanding of how the government builds and pursues cases and strong knowledge of current enforcement priorities," firm chairman Matthew Schwartz said in a statement. Khojasteh in a statement said the firm's "identity is built on elite trial work, crisis management and high-stakes litigation." A Boies Schiller spokesperson said Khojasteh had no further comment. Khojasteh represented the Trump administration in a lawsuit brought by protesters, journalists and clergy members who sued to curb ICE agents' use of tear gas and other anti-riot weapons on people protesting an immigration enforcement push in Chicago. The immigration crackdown, dubbed Operation Midway Blitz, led to thousands of arrests as federal agents clashed with protesters from September until December 2025. Agents shot two people, including one person fatally, and threatened to shoot others, body-cam footage showed. US District Judge Sara Ellis granted an injunction sought by the plaintiffs in November 2025, rejecting arguments by Khojasteh that immigration agents only used force when necessary. The judge said immigration officials' allegations about violent, rioting protesters were contradicted by body camera video and other recordings. An appeals court later [USN:L6N3WM110 TEXT:"paused the order"], finding it impermissibly micromanaged federal law enforcement in the city. The Justice Department has shrunk by more than 8,000 employees since 2025, according to August data from the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. That includes more than 4,000 lawyers who have left since the start of Republican President Donald Trump's second term in January 2025; the government has also hired more than 1,700 lawyers in that time. Boies Schiller last month hired Stuart McCommas, former DOJ chief of staff and former deputy White House counsel to Trump during his second term, as a partner. Other former DOJ officials at the firm include Alison Anderson, who joined in 2023, and Jesse Panuccio, who joined in 2019.

item.title: TSMC expected to report sixth straight quarter of record profit thanks to AI boom
item.description: TSMC, the world's largest manufacturer of advanced AI chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings on Thursday, driven by booming infrastructure spending in the tech sector.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: TSMC, the world's largest manufacturer of advanced AI chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings on Thursday, driven by booming infrastructure spending in the tech sector. Analysts say demand for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co's (TSMC) (2330.TW) AI chipmaking capacity, as well as its advanced chip packaging technology, CoWoS, remains strong. That has catapulted Asia's most valuable company, a key supplier to Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) , to new heights. Its market capitalisation is almost double that of South Korean rival Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) at around $2 trillion. On its Thursday earnings call, TSMC is expected to report a 65% surge in third-quarter net profit to T$746.3 billion ($23.4 billion), according to an LSEG SmartEstimate compiled from 16 analysts. SmartEstimates place greater weight on forecasts from analysts who are more consistently accurate. The call at which it will provide fourth-quarter and updated full-year guidance is scheduled for 0600 GMT. Any result above T$706.56 billion would mark the company's highest-ever quarterly net income, as well as its 11th consecutive quarter of profit growth. Last week, it reported a 50% year-on-year rise in [USN:L6N45U0AF TEXT:"third-quarter revenue"], beating market forecasts and hitting a new record. TSMC is investing $265 billion to build chip factories in the US state of Arizona, including an additional $100 billion that was unveiled in July. In September, Reuters reported that TSMC was [USN:L6N45M06T TEXT:"evaluating"] a potential investment in Texas. Tesla CEO Elon Musk also said last week that his companies would build and operate the Terafab AI chip complex, with TSMC potentially subleasing a part of it. On its July earnings call, the company raised its capex forecast for this year to between $60 billion and $64 billion from a previous prediction at the high end of $52 billion to $56 billion. TSMC's Taipei-listed shares have gained 63% so far this year, broadly in line with a 69% rise for the broader Taiwanese market (.TWII) .

item.title: PT vai à OEA com denúncias de interferência nas eleições pela Meta
item.description: A coordenação de campanha de reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) entrará com uma denúncia na Organização dos Estados Americanos (OEA) contra o que considera manipulação das redes sociais feita pela Meta, empresa dona das redes sociais Instagram, WhatsApp e Facebook, durante a eleição brasileira.
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: A coordenação de campanha de reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) entrará com uma denúncia na Organização dos Estados Americanos (OEA) contra o que considera manipulação das redes sociais feita pela Meta, empresa dona das redes sociais Instagram, WhatsApp e Facebook, durante a eleição brasileira. "Não podemos admitir essa interferência que está ocorrendo, principalmente da Meta", disse o coordenador da campanha, senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE). "Estamos representando junto à OEA para fazer essa denúncia oficial." Nesta quarta, o partido fez também uma reunião com representantes de organizações internacionais para tentar amplificar as denúncias de interferência, e pretende reunir amanhã observadores internacionais que estão no país para acompanhar as eleições. Entre as denúncias contra a Meta que o PT diz estar acontecendo estão, por exemplo, o fato de postagens do presidente aparecerem sem o botão de compartilhar, terem redução de alcance, e stories também impedirem reações e compartilhamentos, além de aparecerem sem áudio ou em velocidade acelerada. De acordo com a campanha, também estão sendo derrubadas sem razão páginas que defendem a candidatura do presidente ou que fazem convocações para atos que estão sendo organizados. Camilo Santana disse, ainda, que buscas feitas por "exército do Lula" -- o canal de WhatsApp criado pelo deputado federal André Janones (Rede-MG) para mobilizar a militância lulista -- levam à "tropa de Flávio", canal do mesmo estilo criado pela campanha do opositor, senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). O partido também inclui ainda a restrição do Meta AI, inteligência artificial da empresa usada no Whatsapp e outras redes da empresa, para criação de imagens em apoio a Lula. Nesse caso, um pedido feito à IA da empresa se recusa a criar imagens com o nome e o número do presidente, enquanto o mesmo pedido feito para Flávio criaria a imagem sem problemas. A campanha já havia entrado com uma representação no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) para contestar os problemas detectados com a Meta. Na resposta ao TSE, a Meta admitiu problemas, mas informou que não teriam sido específicos de materiais da campanha. Em relação às visualizações de conteúdos, a empresa alegou que foi um problema mundial de contagem, que não afetou apenas a campanha de Lula. Também reconheceu que retirou do ar a página da campanha do presidente, mas alega que foi apenas por uma hora, por um problema técnico. A desconfiança de que as chamadas big techs poderiam tentar interferir nas eleições brasileiras era uma constante no governo brasileiro. Mais de uma vez, fontes citaram ocorrências na Colômbia e em Honduras como exemplos, mas reconheceram que era difícil se precaver do que poderia vir a acontecer. Procurados pela Reuters, a Meta disse que não iria comentar e o TSE não deu retorno.

item.title: Martinez stands by Man Utd criticism after Atletico defeat
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has defended his criticism of the club's leadership following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, saying his comments reflected his desire to see the team compete for major honours.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has defended his criticism of the club's leadership following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, saying his comments reflected his desire to see the team compete for major honours. The Argentina international acknowledged that frustration had shaped his [USN:L1N45Z14X TEXT:"post-match remarks"], in which he called for greater investment in the squad and questioned director of football Jason Wilcox's recruitment efforts, but stopped short of apologising. "After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted," Martinez wrote on Instagram on Wednesday. "Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don’t go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United. "My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours." Martinez reiterated that the players also had to take responsibility for improving the team's performances. "I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility," he said. "We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top." The defeat extended United's winless run to five matches in all competitions, adding to the scrutiny surrounding head coach Michael Carrick as the club adjusts to life back in the Champions League after two seasons away. "I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward," Martinez added. "I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment." Reuters has contacted the club for comment. United have not publicly responded to Martinez's remarks, although ESPN and Sky Sports reported that Wilcox retained the backing of the club's leadership.

item.title: Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani in lineup, sixth in batting order
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- For the first time as a member of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shohei Ohtani will be in the No. 6 slot in the batting order on Wednesday when the Dodgers face the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- For the first time as a member of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shohei Ohtani will be in the No. 6 slot in the batting order on Wednesday when the Dodgers face the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series. The slugging Ohtani has not hit sixth since 2020, when he was a member of the Los Angeles Angels. In that COVID-shortened season, Ohtani played in 44 of 60 games and hit only .190 with seven home runs, while dealing with an elbow strain. The Japanese superstar has three singles in 20 at-bats during the 2026 post-season. Milwaukee leads the series, 2-0. Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts revealed on Tuesday that he had discussed the possibility of resting Ohtani against Milwaukee left-hander Robert Gasser in Game 3, but the slugger was "adamant" that he is healthy enough to serve as the designated hitter. Ohtani has been plagued by right biceps and left knee injuries since June. Kyle Tucker moves up five slots from Monday's Game 2 lineup. He's in the cleanup spot. Roberts also moved catcher Will Smith down two spots to seventh and inserted third baseman Miguel Rojas to replace Max Muncy in a righty-for-lefty exchange. Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell will oppose Gasser. The Brewers will again sit Christian Yelich against the southpaw, opting for right-handed hitter Andrew Vaughn, who will serve as the designated hitter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Venezia appoint Nicola as coach
item.description: Venezia have appointed Davide Nicola as head coach on a two-year contract, the Serie A club said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venezia have appointed Davide Nicola as head coach on a two-year contract, the Serie A club said on Wednesday. Nicola replaced Giovanni Stroppa, who was [USN:L4N45Z0QQ TEXT:"dismissed "]on Tuesday with the side rooted to the bottom of the table following six straight league defeats. Stroppa led the club to promotion last season. A specialist in top-flight survival, Nicola, 53, arrives with a record of engineering miraculous escapes, having guided struggling sides including Genoa, Torino and Cagliari to Serie A safety. "I chose Venezia because I see a long-term vision and significant opportunities for growth," Nicola said in a statement. "In my profession, what matters most to me is the ability to create emotions and write chapters of history that will stand the test of time." Nicola's tenure begins when Venezia host Napoli on Saturday looking for their first points of the campaign.

item.title: Serie A sides endure humbling Champions League match day
item.description: Serie A clubs set an unwelcome record on Wednesday as two defeats ensured that all four Italian teams lost on the same Champions League match day for the first time in history.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Serie A clubs set an unwelcome record on Wednesday as two defeats ensured that all four Italian teams lost on the same Champions League match day for the first time in history. AS Roma[USN:L1N46011B TEXT:" were beaten 4-3"] at home by Real Madrid and debutants Como lost 3-2 to Feyenoord in Rotterdam. On Tuesday, Inter Milan [USN:L6N45Z15P TEXT:"went down"] 4-3 at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, and Napoli succumbed to a 3-1 defeat at Villarreal. For Serie A champions Inter, the home setback against Brugge highlighted a stark decline in form. Inter have now lost seven of their last eight Champions League games, a far cry from the side that reached the final in 2023 and 2025. Italian football is in a transitional period following the national team's failure to qualify for the World Cup for a third consecutive tournament. The Italian Football Federation is under the temporary stewardship of special administrator Giovanni Malago after he [USN:L6N45S0QX TEXT:"resigned "]as president this month. Roma looked on course for a famous victory over record 15-times European champions Real as they led 3-1 after a Donyell Malen double. The Italians, however, conceded three goals in the final seven minutes with former Roma defender Antonio Rudiger delivering Madrid's 90th-minute winner. "It has to be a valuable lesson, we need to be fully focused for the full 90 minutes plus stoppages. I think it has to be an issue of mentality, because when you concede three practically identical goals in seven minutes, something is wrong," Roma forward Matias Soule told Amazon Prime. Como manager Cesc Fabregas admitted the elite European competition comes with a steep learning curve after his side suffered a narrow defeat at Feyenoord. "The Champions League is the strongest competition. There is a higher level here than at a World Cup," Fabregas said. "It is a gift for this club and I will keep saying it. We will get there step by step, we have a path to follow. We need to keep cool heads and be consistent."

item.title: Clip atribuido a despedida de Messi de la selección se grabó en celebraciones de Argentina por título mundial en 2022
item.description: Un video de las celebraciones por la victoria de Argentina en la Copa Mundial de la FIFA de diciembre de 2022 en las calles de Buenos Aires se comparte erróneamente como si correspondiera a una multitud por el partido de despedida del futbolista Lionel Messi de la selección “albiceleste” en octubre de 2026.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Un video de las celebraciones por la victoria de Argentina en la Copa Mundial de la FIFA de diciembre de 2022 en las calles de Buenos Aires se comparte erróneamente como si correspondiera a una multitud por el partido de [USN:L1N45S13M TEXT:"despedida"] del futbolista Lionel Messi de la selección “albiceleste” en octubre de 2026. Una publicación en Instagram que incluye el clip con imágenes tomadas desde un punto elevado de multitudes en calles y puentes dice : "Se desata la locura en Argentina por la despedida de Lio Messi". Sin embargo, el video muestra las [USN:L8N33940H TEXT:"celebraciones"] en Buenos Aires el día en el que la selección argentina regresó al país con el trofeo de la Copa Mundial de Qatar en diciembre de 2022. El ejemplo más antiguo visto por Reuters lo publicó en X el 20 de diciembre el usuario @facudelreal. Los medios ESPN Deportes y Fox Soccer lo divulgaron ese día y se lo atribuyeron. Reuters difundió ese día imágenes y una [USN:L8N33940H TEXT:"cápsula"] en las que se ven los mismos edificios y una multitud en Buenos Aires. Consultado el 8 de octubre de 2026 en un mensaje en Instagram, Del Real no comentó sobre la autoría del video. Reuters no pudo verificar de forma independiente el origen. El video fue filmado en las inmediaciones de la autopista 25 de Mayo , en el este de la capital argentina, y una vista en Google Earth del lugar muestra los mismos edificios que se observan en el clip difundido en línea. La selección argentina publicó en X en diciembre de 2023 una cápsula sobre la victoria del país en la Copa Mundial del año anterior e incluyó una escena similar de los festejos. Anteriormente, Reuters abordó publicaciones en árabe que decían erróneamente que el clip correspondía a protestas en California. Reuters publicó fotografías del partido de despedida de la selección argentina de Messi , que se celebró el 6 de octubre de 2026 en el Estadio Monumental de Buenos Aires. El Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. VEREDICTO Erróneamente etiquetado. Un video de celebraciones en Buenos Aires por la victoria de Argentina en el Mundial que se grabó en 2022 es atribuido a imágenes de la despedida de Lionel Messi de la selección argentina en 2026. item.title: Florida can enforce state law barring young kids from social media, appeals court rules
item.description: A federal appeals court on Wednesday allowed Florida to enforce a state law barring children under 14 from accessing social media platforms like Instagram, TikTok or Snapchat, rejecting tech industry groups' claims that the law violates the US Constitution’s free speech protections.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A federal appeals court on Wednesday allowed Florida to enforce a state law barring children under 14 from accessing social media platforms like Instagram, TikTok or Snapchat, rejecting tech industry groups' claims that the law violates the US Constitution’s free speech protections. In a unanimous ruling, a three-judge panel on the Atlanta-based 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals vacated a lower court’s preliminary injunction blocking the law, known as H.B. 3. The court said the law does not regulate the content hosted by social media sites and therefore doesn’t run afoul of the First Amendment. “HB3 applies to platforms wholly without regard to the topics discussed or the ideas or messages conveyed on them,” wrote Circuit Judge Kevin Newsom, an appointee of President Donald Trump. “Truth Social is just as likely as Instagram to be affected by HB3.” Representatives for Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, who defended the law, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The law bars social media platforms that have so-called addictive features, which include things like video autoplay and infinite scroll, from allowing children under the age of 14 to create accounts. Tech industry groups NetChoice and the Computer & Communications Industry Association, which count Meta Platforms, TikTok and Snap as members, had sued in 2024 to block the law. In a statement after the ruling on Wednesday, Paul Taske, director of the NetChoice Litigation Center, said the group is "currently evaluating all of our options as we continue the fight to ensure Floridians’ rights to free expression online are protected, and parents remain in the driver’s seat when it comes to making decisions for their families." SNAP SUED Florida was among the first of several states to pass a law regulating social media use for children amid [USN:L6N3YY121 TEXT:"a broader reckoning"] over the apps’ role in young people’s mental health. After H.B. 3 took effect, Uthmeier sued Snapchat owner [USN:L1N3R0146 TEXT:"Snap Inc"] in April 2025, accusing it of illegally employing features that addict children and opening accounts for children aged 13 and younger. Snap said H.B. 3 and the lawsuit sought to restrict teens' speech online in violation of the US Constitution. A few months later, the judge overseeing the industry groups' lawsuit granted their request for a preliminary injunction blocking the law’s enforcement, saying H.B. 3 was likely unconstitutional. Uthmeier [USN:L6N3ZY17H TEXT:"appealed that ruling"] to the 11th Circuit, and the court had stayed the injunction while it weighed the case. Separately, a lower court overseeing Florida’s case against Snap had rejected the state’s request in August 2025 to order Snap to comply with H.B. 3, also finding the law likely violated constitutional rights. But in a second ruling on Wednesday, the 11th Circuit vacated that decision and said the case should move forward in state court, not federal. A representative for Snap declined to comment. The case is CCIA and NetChoice v. Uthmeier, 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals, number 25-11881. For CCIA and NetChoice: Erin Murphy of Clement & Murphy For Florida: Jeffrey DeSousa of the Florida Attorney General's Office

item.title: At Anthropic pre-IPO meet: ‘Thinking’ caps, surging revenue, no human extinction
item.description: Anthropic told prospective investors on Wednesday that revenue in the third quarter surged 45% from the prior quarter, two people who attended an investor day said, a move that could assuage market concerns about the huge costs of developing AI systems.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn, Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: Anthropic told prospective investors on Wednesday that revenue in the third quarter surged 45% from the prior quarter, two people who attended an investor day said, a move that could assuage market concerns about the huge costs of developing AI systems. Revenue in the third quarter rose to $16.8 billion from $11.6 billion in the second quarter and $4.7 billion in the first quarter, the people said. Anthropic told the group the company was profitable on an adjusted basis in the third quarter, they added. The meeting in San Francisco was meant to familiarize prospective Anthropic investors with the company before its highly anticipated IPO. The IPO is expected to precede a public listing by rival OpenAI, making Anthropic an early test of investor appetite for heavily unprofitable AI developers pursuing massive scale. Its public-market debut is likely to be pushed until after the November US midterm elections , Reuters has reported. Attendees at Wednesday's event met with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao and came away optimistic about the company's rapid revenue growth and path to profitability, a few of them told Reuters as they left its headquarters in the evening. Amodei reiterated the company’s focus on AI safety but avoided mentioning threats of human extinction, one person in the group said. In its prospectus seen by Reuters last month, Anthropic warned that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"existential risks to humanity"]." On Wednesday, however, Anthropic executives talked about how the company was using its AI to help its own business including designing a custom chip. The company handed out hats to the attendees, some of which read "thinking." The company is expecting a $110 billion annual revenue run rate by the end of the year, another person who attended the event said. Anthropic did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment. Scrutiny of AI companies' finances has intensified as they pour money into chips, data centers and computing power needed to develop and operate increasingly powerful models. Targeting a valuation of over $2 trillion, Anthropic is seeking to convince investors that its breakneck revenue growth can eventually outrun the enormous costs of building and running AI systems. Last year, Anthropic's revenue increased [USN:L6N45L00B TEXT:"twelvefold to"] nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, excluding writedowns of various liabilities mostly tied to previous fundraising, Reuters reported exclusively last month. The company has committed at least [USN:L1N45K0RM TEXT:"$518 billion over a decade"] for cloud services, computing and infrastructure. Founded by former OpenAI executives, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. Its expansion has been underpinned by Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and Amazon (AMZN.O) , which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as AI competitors. Anthropic has also sought to distinguish itself through its focus on AI safety, warning of the dangers posed by increasingly capable systems even as it competes in the race to develop and commercialize more powerful models. Its research has found that its own AI agents have engaged in troubling behavior in test environments, including leaking sensitive information and sabotaging code, though the company has said it has not seen evidence of such misalignment in real-world deployments. The Financial Times first reported the third-quarter revenue figure on Wednesday.

item.title: Haaland leads City fightback but Maresca tastes first defeat
item.description: Manchester City's 4-2 defeat by Paris St Germain told only part of the story of Enzo Maresca's first loss as City boss, with his men staggering through the first half before roaring back after the break.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City's 4-2 defeat by Paris St Germain told only part of the story of Enzo Maresca's first loss as City boss, with his men staggering through the first half before roaring back after the break. Playing their first home game since an independent commission found them guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules, City were staring at a rout when a rampant PSG raced into a 3-0 lead with a first-half masterclass. Then City woke up. Maresca's side tore into the visitors after halftime, pouring forward with an intensity and urgency that had been entirely absent in the opening 45 minutes. Erling Haaland spearheaded the fightback, scoring twice to become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the mark in just 60 games, 20 quicker than Lionel Messi. City kept coming. They finished with nearly twice as many shots as PSG and around three times as many touches in the opposition box, while recording a higher expected-goals figure at both halftime and fulltime. PSG, though, were more ruthless. "I think we start quite good until the first goal (from Desire Doue in the 13th minute) and then we concede the second one (Ousmane Dembele) after one minute. That created some bad feelings," Maresca told TNT Sports. "Second half, we were much better and probably deserved something more." City had arrived on the back of a 3-0 thrashing of Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday and Maresca felt they generated enough chances to salvage something even after digging themselves a three-goal hole. "Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more," he said. "Luis (Enrique, PSG's manager) said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky today. "You have to be clinical but not lose the balance," Maresca said. The defeat unfolded against a backdrop of turmoil stretching far beyond City, with the fallout from the seismic verdict over the 114 breaches sending shockwaves through the Premier League and making City the villains of English football in the eyes of many. They have denied wrongdoing and have appealed. On the pitch, they remain three points clear of Arsenal atop the Premier League table ahead of Saturday's home game against Ipswich. Asked if he had a message for supporters, Maresca said: "We are sorry for the first half for sure. Saturday is a Premier League game and we need to continue our run."
