Here are some details: The company's deal backlog is large enough to more than support its debt obligations, Intrator told employees in a memo that was seen by Reuters Issues such as the difficulties and delays observed in the attempted IPOs and debt financings of some of CoreWeave's rivals "are bleeding into the narrative around CoreWeave", Intrator said in the memo According to Bloomberg News, which first reported on the remarks earlier in the day, CoreWeave's bonds have plunged to levels that typically indicate distress CoreWeave's unsecured debt due in 2032 traded below 80 cents on the dollar on Wednesday, Bloomberg News said in a separate report citing Trace pricing data CoreWeave has reported revenue [USN:L4N4481ER TEXT:"backlog of $104.2 billion"] in the second quarter, up from $99.4 billion in the first quarter On top of the backlog, the company said it had secured more than $25 billion of net new customer commitments in the third quarter

item.title: Nasdaq fecha com forte queda, conforme dados sobre inflação alimentam temores de alta dos juros
item.description: Dados de inflação acima do esperado levaram o Nasdaq a um fechamento em forte queda nesta quarta-feira, com as preocupações sobre novos aumentos nas taxas de juros pelo Federal Reserve prejudicando as ações da Oracle, da CoreWeave e de outras empresas de IA sensíveis ao aumento dos custos de financiamento.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: Dados de inflação acima do esperado levaram o Nasdaq a um fechamento em forte queda nesta quarta-feira, com as preocupações sobre novos aumentos nas taxas de juros pelo Federal Reserve prejudicando as ações da Oracle, da CoreWeave e de outras empresas de IA sensíveis ao aumento dos custos de financiamento. O aumento das apostas de que o Fed precisará de mais aumentos nas taxas para conter a inflação representou um duro golpe para algumas das empresas que mais valorizaram no mercado em 2026. A Oracle (ORCL.N) tombou 8,8%, enquanto as empresas de infraestrutura de IA CoreWeave (CRWV.O) e Nebius (NBIS.O) despencaram 15% e 10%, respectivamente. A Dell (DELL.N) e a Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE.N) caíram 11,4% e 8,2%, respectivamente, depois que o Barclays rebaixou a recomendação das fabricantes de servidores de IA de acima da média do mercado para neutro. O Índice de chips da Philadelphia SE (.SOX) caiu 4,3%, registrando queda pela sexta sessão consecutiva — sua maior sequência de perdas desde maio de 2025. Os preços ao consumidor nos EUA aceleraram em setembro, à medida que o custo da gasolina disparou e as pressões sobre os preços se estenderam para além do setor de energia, segundo dados do Bureau de Estatísticas do Trabalho do Departamento do Trabalho. Os operadores de taxas de juros estão precificando uma probabilidade de 37% de que os formuladores de política monetária do Fed aumentem as taxas neste mês, ante 22% na terça-feira, de acordo com a ferramenta FedWatch da CME. “Os investidores não estão satisfeitos com o relatório porque isso pressiona o Fed a aumentar as taxas para combater a inflação”, disse Adam Sarhan, diretor executivo da 50 Park Investments, em Nova York. “A inflação continua sendo o inimigo público número um para o mercado e para o Fed.” O S&P 500 recuou 1,11%, encerrando o pregão em 7.718,94 pontos, sua maior queda em um único dia desde 29 de julho. O Nasdaq caiu 1,88%, para 26.692,87 pontos, sua maior queda diária desde 23 de julho. O Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average teve queda de 0,09%, para 51.621,48 pontos. Oito dos 11 índices setoriais do S&P 500 registraram queda, liderados pelo setor de tecnologia da informação (.SPLRCT) , com baixa de 2,6%, seguido por uma perda de 1,78% no setor de serviços de comunicação (.SPLRCL) . Depois de atingir uma alta recorde na semana passada, o S&P 500 continua com alta de quase 13% em 2026, com a maior parte desse ganho impulsionado por ações relacionadas à IA. A mediana das ações do S&P 500 subiu 4% em 2026, e mais de 200 dos componentes do índice estão em território negativo. O Bank of America (BAC.N) caiu 4,8%. O lucro do banco diminuiu no terceiro trimestre, pois ele reservou US$1,2 bilhão para cobrir multas regulatórias por falhas na detecção de possíveis casos de lavagem de dinheiro. O Morgan Stanley (MS.N) caiu quase 3%, apesar de um aumento no lucro trimestral. O índice S&P 500 Banks (.SPXBK) recuou 0,7%, atingindo seu menor fechamento desde junho. Antes da divulgação dos dados sobre a inflação, a vice-chair de Supervisão do Fed, Michelle Bowman, afirmou que o banco central tinha tempo para aguardar e observar como os mercados e a economia evoluiriam após o aumento da taxa de juros em setembro, antes de decidir sobre novas medidas. A Bending Spoons (BSP.O) disparou 41% depois que a Berkshire Hathaway (BRKa.N) investiu mais US$330 milhões na proprietária do Vimeo e da AOL — um grande endosso do investidor de grande visibilidade, cujos movimentos são acompanhados de perto pelos operadores de mercado.

item.title: Anthropic to add US voting information to Claude before midterms
item.description: Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the November midterms.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the November midterms. The AI company said its goal was to position Claude as a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse. "Today, conversations that touch broadly on politics, public policy or social issues account for about 5.75% of all conversations in the United States on Claude.ai, our consumer app," the company said in a statement, citing analysis of 250,000 US conversations. The move comes as AI companies increasingly position chatbots as sources of news and information, potentially helping Anthropic draw more users during the election cycle. About 0.51% of Claude conversations are specifically about elections or voting, Anthropic said, adding that it expects political and election-related queries to rise as election day approaches. Later this month, US users seeking voting logistics will receive answers drawn directly from Democracy Works’ database of state and local election sources. Anthropic said requests for recommendations on how to vote were extremely rare, accounting for just 0.01% of U.S. conversations.

item.title: Perella Weinberg, Piper Sandler abandon merger talks, source says
item.description: Investment bank Piper Sandler and advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners have abandoned talks for an all-stock merger as they could not agree on financial and personnel terms, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Abigail Summerville
item.content:encoded: Investment bank Piper Sandler (PIPR.N) and advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners (PWP.O) have abandoned talks for an all-stock merger as they could not agree on financial and personnel terms, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday. Shares of Perella Weinberg closed 19.1% lower at $13, while those of Piper Sandler ended up 0.96% at $64.5. Perella Weinberg declined to comment, while Piper Sandler did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Financial Times first reported on Wednesday that the merger talks fell through. The Wall Street Journal had reported last month that Piper Sandler was in talks to buy Perella Weinberg, which had a market value of about $1.4 billion at the time. A $485-million merger between Minneapolis-based Piper Jaffray and New York-based Sandler O'Neill led to the formation of Piper Sandler Companies in January 2020, creating a major investment bank specializing in the middle market, with leading advisory practices in financial services, healthcare and energy. Meanwhile, Perella Weinberg was founded by veteran Wall Street bankers Joseph Perella, Peter Weinberg and Terry Meguid in 2006. The firm went public in 2021 through a merger with a blank-check company backed by banking entrepreneur Betsy Cohen, in a deal valued at about $975 million.

item.title: Fed's Goolsbee says September CPI data was discouraging - Yahoo Finance
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Wednesday the latest consumer-level inflation data left him worried about the state of price pressures.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Wednesday the latest consumer-level inflation data left him worried about the state of price pressures. The September [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer price index"] data, which showed higher-than-expected price pressures, was “discouraging,” Goolsbee said in an interview with Yahoo Finance. When it comes to the price pressure data, “I'm concerned, related to not just the overall number, but if you break out the components, services inflation shows little sign of improvement,” the official said, while affirming the central bank will get inflation back to its 2% target. Goolsbee stopped short of saying how he thinks the central bank should respond with rate policy in the near term while saying in strong terms that the Fed can't allow high price pressures to persist. If inflation pressures remain elevated, "there's not ambiguity about what, how the central bank has to deal with that," he said. "You must prevent the buildup of overheating, because if you get overheating buildup on the demand side, that tends to be very persistent and hard to get rid of," Goolsbee said. The Fed raised its interest rate target by a quarter percentage point last month to between 3.75% and 4% and penciled in an additional increase by the end of the year, as it works to get inflation to its 2% target. Key Fed officials have [USN:S0N44V01O TEXT:"waved"] markets off expectations of a rate hike at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting set for the end of the month, though the release of the CPI data put new life into market expectations that the central bank may move again sooner rather than later. In the interview, Goolsbee explained that the inflation data showed that price pressures are high even in the areas outside those directly impacted by things like tariffs, which is in part why he found the latest report to be so vexing. "This month's reading is over 5% for services inflation and you can't really attribute services inflation to tariffs, to oil prices, or things like that," Goolsbee said. "On the ground here in the Midwest, everywhere we're going, we're hearing about costs and we're hearing about prices," Goolsbee said. "There's very little that we're hearing that sounds like downturn, risks of recession and things like that, so that makes you more nervous about demand side overheating than just straight supply shock." The Fed has failed to get inflation back to its 2% target for over five years, though officials say market and public expectations data shows continued confidence that price pressures will be brought under control.

item.title: What is Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink?
item.description: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's SpaceX had restricted military-grade Starlink services, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"SpaceX had restricted "military-grade" Starlink services"], hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses. The complaint has drawn renewed attention to the distinction between Starlink, SpaceX's commercial satellite internet service, and Starshield, a military version developed for the Pentagon. While Musk has said the two systems are separate, in many cases they share the same underlying satellite technology. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government," Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X, adding that any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military or the president. "Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company." WHAT IS STARLINK? Starlink, the main profit engine of SpaceX (SPCX.O) , is a satellite internet network of more than 11,000 satellites that beam broadband service directly to user terminals about the size of a folded newspaper. Its roughly 13 million subscribers range from households and hikers to shipping companies and major airlines. Since launching its first Starlink satellites in 2019 aboard reusable SpaceX rockets, the company has built a vast low-Earth-orbit constellation that blankets much of the planet, delivering faster connections than traditional communications satellites, which typically operate much farther from Earth and in far smaller numbers. Starlink gave Ukraine a critical communications advantage early in the war, reshaping how militaries operate on the battlefield. But Musk has restricted Starlink for certain military uses while highlighting Starshield, a more secure network developed for government and military missions. WHAT IS STARSHIELD? Starshield is a SpaceX business unit that develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the Pentagon. While its missions are separate from Starlink's commercial broadband service, the distinction is not always clear-cut: Starshield's secure communications services use enhanced encryption and dedicated terminals, but rely on the vast Starlink constellation as their backbone. Starshield leverages the technology, engineering and operational experiences of Starlink, according to SpaceX. In addition to secure communications, the company says the militarized version can also provide users with Earth observation and the ability to integrate sensors or other payloads. The Pentagon, Starshield's largest customer, has spent billions of dollars on both Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft for missile-warning missions and a spy constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office, Reuters reported in 2024. Questions over the relationship between Starlink and Starshield have persisted since [USN:L1N31S38K TEXT:"Russia threatened Western satellites supporting Ukraine in 2022"]. SpaceX unveiled Starshield later that year, but the secrecy surrounding national security space programs has left the precise boundaries between the two systems opaque. Those distinctions became a point of contention earlier this year when the [USN:L6N41W1B2 TEXT:"Pentagon clashed with SpaceX over higher prices for satellite services"] used by military drones during the Iran conflict, Reuters reported. SpaceX argued that some customers paying roughly $5,000 per terminal for Starlink should instead have been using a Starshield service costing about $25,000 per terminal. [USN:L6N4290XG TEXT:"Britain has also adopted Starshield"]. Under that arrangement, the service uses the same satellite constellation, ground stations and terrestrial infrastructure as Starlink, but operates through dedicated terminals and separate network gateways, Britain’s defence ministry has told Reuters. Other US partners are evaluating the system as well. New Zealand is doing a trial of Starshield to assess its usefulness for military operations, the New Zealand Defence Force previously told Reuters.

item.title: Former portfolio manager sues Fidelity after leaving for Michael Dell's family office
item.description: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne McGee
item.content:encoded: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies (DELL.N) founder Michael Dell. The suit, filed by Adam Benjamin in the Suffolk Division of the Superior Court of Massachusetts, alleges that after Fidelity executives failed to persuade him to stay at the firm, the company "turned on a dime" and terminated him on July 10 of this year. Fidelity then imposed a non-compete clause, causing him to forfeit a compensation package totaling in the millions of dollars. "Rather than protecting any legitimate business interests, the provisions are being broadly misused by Fidelity as a retention tool or improper barrier/deterrent to" Benjamin's ability to pursue other professional opportunities, the lawsuit alleges. Fidelity declined to comment on the lawsuit, which was filed on Friday. Neither Benjamin nor his lawyers could be reached for comment. Non-compete agreements are common in the asset management industry. Benjamin managed the $48 billion Fidelity Select Semiconductors Portfolio, which is up 58% so far this year, compared to 13.3% for the S&P 500 (.SPX) index. Its average annual return of 37.4% over the last five years puts it in the top percentile of all comparable funds rated by Morningstar, which awarded the fund five stars and a gold medalist rating, its top score. Benjamin began working at DFO on October 1, the lawsuit said. He alleged that Fidelity's withholding of compensation rests on the false claim that he was joining a competitor. He said he has never worked for Fidelity's own family office business.

item.title: Bond trading weakens for US banks as interest rate volatility affects investors
item.description: A steep selloff in the bond market showed up in Wall Street bank earnings during the last quarter, with some banks showing weaker fixed income trading as high interest rate volatility during the quarter curbed demand for transactions.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Bautzer
item.content:encoded: A steep [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"selloff in the bond market"] showed up in Wall Street bank earnings during the last quarter, with some banks showing weaker fixed income trading as high interest rate volatility during the quarter curbed demand for transactions. During the quarter, Treasury yields reached [USN:L6N45S11R TEXT:"multi-decade highs"] with some days showing abrupt moves in the market as investors repriced their expectations for where interest rates will go. At Morgan Stanley, revenues from fixed income, currencies and commodities trading (FICC) fell 7% in the quarter from a year earlier. [USN:L4N45Z0V1 TEXT:"At JPMorgan"], the drop was 4% and at [USN:L4N4600WF TEXT:"Bank of America"], 17%. [USN:L4N45Z0U6 TEXT:"Goldman Sachs"] had flat revenues with FICC trading. Citi was the odd one out, increasing its revenue 4% from a year earlier. "Interest rates rose pretty furiously throughout the third quarter, and it was unexpected versus where the market was in the second quarter", said Morgan Stanley Chief Financial Officer Sharon Yeshaya. There was less demand for structured transactions and the widening of credit spreads was a challenge to investors that have bond portfolios. Benchmark 10-year yields showed their [USN:L6N45M19U TEXT:"biggest quarterly rise since 2009"] at the end of September. "Reduced client activity and changing market conditions, including a major shift in interest rates, significantly affected our leading FICC businesses, including credit, mortgages and municipals," according to Bank of America Chief Financial Officer Alastair Borthwick. At Citigroup, most of the 4% growth in FICC trading revenue came from foreign exchange business and spread products. Citi CEO Jane Fraser told analysts rates revenue "was pressured by the trading environment, but we saw good growth in forex and spread products, both stable revenue streams." Another effect of [USN:L1N45U12M TEXT:"rising long-term yields"] on the banks' balance sheets was the higher volume of unrealized losses in securities portfolios. [USN:L4N4600XY TEXT:"Bank of America, for example"], showed unrealized losses on its bond portfolio - mortgage-backed securities and US Treasury, government-agency bonds - at $109 billion in the quarter ended September, up from $85 billion at the end of June, as bond yields rose in the last quarter. The bulk of these securities were in held-to-maturity segment, which the bank does not intend to sell. EQUITIES SHINE The results contrasted with that from equities trading desks, which brought eye-popping revenue growth in the quarter. At Goldman Sachs, equity trading revenue rose 72%, with higher revenues in derivatives and financing. Morgan Stanley equity revenues grew 41% and JPMorgan's, 49%. Bank of America and Citi had the lowest equity trading revenues growth, 11% and 14%, respectively. Oppenheimer analyst Chris Kotowski sees increased risk in the reliance on equity revenues, that may be volatile. "We do fear that there is an 'easy come, easy go' risk with these revenues," he wrote in a note to clients.

item.title: PSG down Man City 4-2 in pulsating Champions League clash
item.description: Twice-defending champions Paris St Germain beat Manchester City 4-2 in a pulsating Champions League encounter on Wednesday, their devastating first-half display proving decisive against a City side playing under a cloud of scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Twice-defending champions Paris St Germain beat Manchester City 4-2 in a pulsating Champions League encounter on Wednesday, their devastating first-half display proving decisive against a City side playing under a cloud of scrutiny. On a breathless night featuring 46 goals, Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick in Liverpool's 6-3 thrashing of LASK, Aston Villa recorded the biggest European victory in their history with a 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce and Real Madrid staged a stunning late comeback to beat AS Roma 4-3. But no fixture carried more intrigue than the Etihad clash, where City played their first home game since being found guilty of 114 breaches of financial rules. City, who have denied all wrongdoing and appealed the verdict, were carved open by PSG in the first half. PSG'S FIRST-HALF BLITZ Desire Doue and Ousmane Dembele scored less than two minutes apart before Warren Zaire-Emery's clever touch released Vitinha to drive the third beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 32nd minute. City emerged transformed after the break and Erling Haaland headed in Iliman Ndiaye's cross in the 53rd minute to become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the landmark in 60 games compared with Lionel Messi’s previous record of 80. City's joy was short-lived as Maghnes Akliouche's stunning long-range strike found the net despite Donnarumma getting a hand to it. Haaland had the City fans on their feet when he swept home Ayyoub Bouaddi's pass in the 75th minute for his second, before Donnarumma made up for his blunder by saving a penalty from Ferran Torres. The match unfolded against an "us against the world" backdrop, with City fans in the South Stand holding up cards that read "CTID" (City Till I Die). Former City manager Pep Guardiola watched from the stands alongside chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and senior executives Ferran Soriano and Hugo Viana. VILLA HIT FENERBAHCE FOR SIX At Villa Park, Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both scored twice in a dominant display by the hosts. Johan Manzambi opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Jackson struck in the 31st and 39th minutes to give Villa a commanding halftime lead. Barkley added a fourth from the penalty spot in the 68th minute before grabbing his second four minutes later, while Tammy Abraham completed the rout with a stoppage-time strike. At the Stadio Olimpico, Real Madrid scored three times in the closing stages to overturn a two-goal deficit. Marten de Roon gave Roma the lead in the 20th minute before Kylian Mbappe equalised five minutes later, but Donyell Malen struck twice in the 51st and 57th minutes to put the hosts in control. However, the visitors mounted a remarkable comeback as Carlos Espi pulled a goal back in the 82nd minute before Endrick levelled three minutes later. Former Roma defender Antonio Ruediger then completed the turnaround in the 90th minute, holding off his marker to steer home Arda Guler's inswinging corner from close range and snatch victory for the Spanish side. Liverpool's Barcola, meanwhile, scored his first goals for the club with his hat-trick in their rout of Champions League newcomers LASK in Austria. Ronald Araujo, Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also scored for Andoni Iraola's side, who bounced back from Sunday's 3-0 Premier League defeat by City. Florian Flecker struck twice for the hosts.

item.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms young users
item.description: A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others. Attorneys general from the states, which include Iowa, Kansas and Arizona, filed the lawsuits independently in state courts, claiming ChatGPT is designed to be agreeable and engaging to earn the trust of users. But the chatbot reinforces delusions, encourages dangerous behavior and assists users in planning violence like mass shootings, the lawsuits claim. The lawsuits represent the most significant coordinated state action against an artificial intelligence company, adding to a wave of legal challenges OpenAI faces as it prepares for a public listing. Florida's attorney general filed the first such state [USN:L6N429106 TEXT:"suit"] in June. The lawsuits accuse the company of violating state consumer protection laws by misleading users about the safety of ChatGPT. The states also allege that the company created a public nuisance by endangering the health of their residents. The lawsuits seek orders forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works. Among other things, the states want the company barred from developing AI models that can improve themselves unless it can ensure those models are aligned with human values. The states, which also include Arkansas, Idaho, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia, are also seeking civil monetary penalties for OpenAI's violations of state law as well as damages. A spokesperson for OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The company is also facing dozens of lawsuits by private plaintiffs, alleging ChatGPT helped users [USN:L6N45D0ZP TEXT:"plan mass shootings"] or other violence.

item.title: Racial employment gap widened among new US lawyers, study finds
item.description: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show. More than 94% of 2025’s white law graduates found jobs within 10 months, compared to less than 91% of law graduates of color, according to figures released Wednesday by the National Association for Law Placement. Black law graduates had the lowest employment rate at 87%, down from nearly 90% in 2024, the NALP data showed. The employment rate for 2025 Hispanic law graduates was slightly over 91%, down from more than 92% the previous year. The employment rate for Asian law graduates held steady at about 92%. The relatively small cohort of Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander law graduates posted the highest employment rate at more than 96%. “A law degree should open doors, but NALP's latest report shows that those doors are not equally open to everyone,” NALP Executive Director Nikia Gray said in a statement after releasing the data. The law graduates of 2025 hit the job market amid the Trump administration’s widespread campaign to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion programs in higher education, government and the private sector. In March 2025, the US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission [USN:L1N3Q010H TEXT:"demanded detailed hiring data from 20 major firms"], including applicant names and whether race or gender influenced their employment decisions. The US Federal Trade Commission earlier this year [USN:FWN3YV125 TEXT:"warned"] 42 major law firms that their hiring practices may violate federal antitrust law. Diversity Lab, a group that promoted diversity goals at law firms, [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"shuttered"] in June after coming under FTC scrutiny. Many major law firms have publicly withdrawn or altered their public references to diversity, equity and inclusion since Trump returned to the White House, a Reuters special report found . Nearly 50 US law firms that previously provided NALP with demographic data about their lawyers [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"declined to do so"] this year, with NALP attributing the drop to Trump’s crackdown on law firm DEI efforts. Additionally, the US Department of Education is [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"poised to revoke"] the American Bar Association’s status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools, partly because it says the ABA took too long to eliminate DEI standards for schools. According to the new NALP data, white law graduates outpaced every racial group except for Middle Eastern or North African law graduates in securing jobs that require passing the bar — considered the gold standard for legal employment. First-generation college students had a lower employment rate than law graduates whose parents attended college or law school. Read more: [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"Facing DEI pressures, some law firms shield data in latest diversity survey"] [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"Law firm diversity group shutters amid Trump's DEI crackdown"]

item.title: Patriots open window for A.J. Brown; Christian Gonzalez also limited in return
item.description: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown was a limited participant on Wednesday as the team opened his 21-day practice window.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown was a limited participant on Wednesday as the team opened his 21-day practice window. Brown has been sidelined since sustaining a high-ankle sprain during the second half of the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the teams' season opener on Sept. 9. He went on injured reserve two days later and missed the team's last four games. Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez also was limited after telling reporters before practice that he's ready to return to the field after missing two games due to a shoulder injury. "I'm good now, ready for Sunday," Gonzalez told reporters. The Patriots (3-2) host their AFC East rivals, the New York Jets (2-3), on Sunday. New England cornerbacks Carlton Davis III (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) were the only players who did not practice, while quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder) was a full participant. Brown and Gonzalez were among 13 players listed as limited, including running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and offensive tackles Will Campbell (knee) and Morgan Moses (foot). Gonzalez, 24, signed a four-year, $135 million contract extension last month. He has started all 37 career games in which he has played -- including three this season -- since being selected by New England with the 17th overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Oregon. As for Brown, he sustained his injury after he was targeted by a third-down pass from Maye, but Seahawks nickel cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett deflected the pass to force a punt. Pritchett's knee landed on the outside of Brown's ankle, which twisted inward as he went to the ground. Acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles via trade in early June, Brown had three receptions for a team-high 26 yards in the first half. Brown, 29, was named second-team All-Pro with the Eagles in 2022, 2023 and 2024. He has 527 receptions for 8,055 yards and 56 touchdowns in 106 career games (98 starts) with the Tennessee Titans (2019-21), Eagles (2022-25) and Patriots. --Field Level Media

item.title: South Africa revises rules around customisation of weight-loss drugs
item.description: South Africa is revising its rules governing the customisation of medicines, including sought-after GLP-1 treatments for diabetes and weight loss, health regulators said, warning pharmacies not to act as small-scale manufacturers.
item.dc:creator: Nqobile Dludla
item.content:encoded: South Africa is revising its rules governing the customisation of medicines, including sought-after GLP-1 treatments for diabetes and weight loss, health regulators said, warning pharmacies not to act as small-scale manufacturers. At a multi-stakeholder roundtable on counterfeit medicines on Wednesday, South African Pharmacy Council Registrar and CEO Vincent Tlala said the council was working with the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) on updated minimum standards and guidelines for compounding medicines. The revised standards are expected to go before the council in February, with publication targeted for March. Updated SAHPRA guidelines are expected to be released at the same time, Tlala said. The popularity of GLP-1 medicines such as Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) Ozempic and Wegovy and Eli Lilly's (LLY.N) Mounjaro and Zepbound has fuelled growth in compounded versions, drawing [USN:L8N43B1FF TEXT:"scrutiny"] from regulators [USN:L4N42O23Q TEXT:"globally"]. Compounding refers to the preparation of customised medicines by pharmacists for patients needing a variation to a commercially available product. Tlala said the council was concerned pharmacies were compounding medicines in anticipation of demand rather than for specific patients. "What we are seeing in the market, and which we are against, is when pharmacies become small-scale manufacturers," he said. Authorities are concerned that large-scale compounding may create openings for counterfeit medicines, particularly in high-demand categories such as weight-loss drugs. "There is a scourge of compounded products, especially in the area of weight-loss," Daphney Fafudi, SAHPRA's senior manager for market control, told Reuters on the sidelines. Fafudi said the updated guidelines from SAHPRA and revised minimum standards from the pharmacy council were intended to provide greater clarity on what is and is not permissible when compounding medicines. While existing regulations already contain provisions governing compounding, differing interpretations of those rules have led to disputes within the industry, including [USN:L1N42U0BN TEXT:"litigation"] involving local pharmaceutical compounding company iDexis and Novo Nordisk.

item.title: Baicha Baidao notes Hong Kong regulator's trading suspension over IPO rigging concerns
item.description: China's Sichuan Baicha Baidao Industrial on Wednesday noted the Hong Kong securities regulator's decision to suspend trading over concerns its initial public offering demand may have been rigged.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's Sichuan Baicha Baidao Industrial (2555.HK) on Wednesday noted the Hong Kong securities regulator's decision to suspend trading over concerns its initial public offering demand may have been rigged. Here are some details: The Securities and Futures Commission directed the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong on Tuesday to suspend the Chinese tea shop chain's H shares, citing "serious concerns" about artificial demand for the IPO. "We are acting decisively to protect investors and uphold the integrity of Hong Kong's markets," SFC Executive Director of Enforcement Michael Duignan said. The company, which raised about $330 million in its 2024 Hong Kong debut, said it is seeking legal advice and will work to address and resolve the SFC's concerns. It said that business operations remain normal as of October 14. IPOs and other share sales have become a key regulatory focus this year, with banks and advisers urged to "consider market capacity and choose quality issuers while exercising robust internal control," according to [USN:L8N4520JP TEXT:"two sources"] who spoke to Reuters in September. The sources added that Hong Kong's securities watchdog has also guided investment banks on how to cooperate during regulatory raids.

item.title: México obliga a plataformas digitales a proteger a menores de contenidos nocivos
item.description: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, firmó el miércoles un decreto que obliga a las plataformas digitales a proteger a los niños y adolescentes de contenidos violentos, sexuales y de otras conductas de riesgo, una medida que podría abrir un nuevo frente de regulación para las grandes empresas tecnológicas en uno de los mayores mercados de internet de América Latina.
item.dc:creator: Diego Oré, Raul Cortes
item.content:encoded: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, firmó el miércoles un decreto que obliga a las plataformas digitales a proteger a los niños y adolescentes de contenidos violentos, sexuales y de otras conductas de riesgo, una medida que podría abrir un nuevo frente de regulación para las grandes empresas tecnológicas en uno de los mayores mercados de internet de América Latina. Las plataformas deberán impedir que menores tengan acceso o sean expuestos a contenidos vinculados con discursos de odio, extremismo, abuso, explotación o violencia sexual, suicidio, trastornos alimenticios, acoso y conductas ilícitas, entre otros, según el decreto. "Las plataformas estuvieron de acuerdo, lo único que pidieron fue un mes para poder prepararse para que esto sea una realidad", dijo Sheinbaum en su conferencia de prensa matutina antes de firmar la resolución. El plazo fue acordado en conversaciones entre funcionarios y representantes de Meta, Microsoft, Apple, TikTok, Google, X y Huawei, con los que se consensuó el contenido del decreto, detalló la consejera jurídica de la Presidencia, Luisa María Alcalde. Apple, Microsoft, X, TikTok, Alphabet (propietario de Google y YouTube) y Huawei no respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. "Es obligatorio (el decreto), mas no punitivo, pero creemos que va a ser muy útil", explicó Alcalde. Sin embargo, Sheinbaum agregó que si las empresas no cumplen con las medidas señaladas, el Gobierno publicará una ley que implicará sanciones para ellas. La iniciativa fue anunciada originalmente a principios de octubre, luego que un [USN:L6N45N132 TEXT:"ataque en una escuela"] secundaria en el estado norteño Coahuila dejara un fallecido y tres heridos. Además, forma parte de una estrategia más amplia del gobierno de Sheinbaum para promover entornos digitales seguros para menores. Funcionarios han dicho que las empresas deberán desarrollar mecanismos para identificar y retirar contenidos prohibidos, clasificar materiales por edad, reforzar controles parentales y mantener canales de contacto con autoridades. Un portavoz de Meta (matriz de Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp y Threads) dijo a Reuters que la empresa está "al tanto del anuncio" y que "lo analizarían a detalle", y agregó que desde hace años cuentan con herramientas para que madres y padres acompañen "la experiencia digital de sus hijos". Meta comentó que, además, ofrecen mecanismos de seguridad en sus plataformas como "cuentas de adolescentes en Facebook e Instagram que incluyen protecciones para limitar quién puede contactarlos y el contenido que ven". La propuesta coloca a México en línea con una tendencia internacional hacia una mayor supervisión de las plataformas digitales. En los últimos años, gobiernos de la Unión Europea, Reino Unido, Australia y varios estados de Estados Unidos han impulsado normas para proteger a los menores en internet, exigiendo mayores controles sobre algoritmos, moderación de contenidos y verificación de edad. Iniciativas similares han surgido en América Latina, donde países como Brasil y Colombia han avanzado debates regulatorios para reforzar la protección de menores y exigir mayores responsabilidades a las plataformas digitales. Sin embargo, iniciativas similares han generado debates sobre los límites entre la protección de menores, la privacidad y la libertad de expresión. Sheinbaum ha dicho que el objetivo es responsabilizar a las empresas por los contenidos que difunden a menores y no promover la censura. La atención de inversionistas y expertos del sector estará puesta en la implementación del decreto, incluyendo los mecanismos de cumplimiento y la eventual respuesta de las empresas implicadas. Cualquier endurecimiento regulatorio podría convertirse en un precedente para futuras normas sobre seguridad digital y contenido en México, el segundo mercado de internet más grande de América Latina después de Brasil.

item.title: Dólar toca máximo en 18 meses, luego cede ciertas alzas ya que inversores apuestas por una Fed paciente
item.description: El dólar tocó el miércoles su máximo en 18 meses, luego de que datos de inflación superiores a lo esperado reavivaran brevemente las expectativas de un alza de tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal este mes, pero la moneda luego se dio un respiro ya que los inversores volvieron a la creencia de que la Fed será paciente.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: El dólar tocó el miércoles su máximo en 18 meses, luego de que datos de inflación superiores a lo esperado reavivaran brevemente las expectativas de un alza de tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal este mes, pero la moneda luego se dio un respiro ya que los inversores volvieron a la creencia de que la Fed será paciente. La Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales del Departamento de Trabajo informó el miércoles de que los precios al consumidor en Estados Unidos subieron considerablemente en septiembre debido al fuerte repunte de los precios de la gasolina. El índice dólar , que mide la fortaleza del billete verde frente a una cesta de seis divisas, subió un 0,34%, a 102,53 unidades, después de cotizar previamente hasta los 102,94 puntos. El informe eclipsó las recientes señales moderadas de los responsables de la Fed, incluidos los comentarios del presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams, que debilitaron al dólar el martes. La vicepresidenta de Supervisión de la Fed, Michelle Bowman, también señaló un enfoque de esperar y ver antes de subir nuevamente el costo del crédito. Mientras, el Libre Beige del banco central estadounidense mostró el miércoles que el mercado laboral se mantenía en patrón de baja contratación y bajos despidos, mientras que las presiones inflacionarias aumentaron en partes del país. Los operadores estiman ahora que hay un 65% de probabilidades de que la Fed mantenga las tasas sin cambios en su reunión del 27 al 28 de octubre, frente al 53% de hace un mes, mientras que descuentan un endurecimiento de unos 79 puntos básicos para finales de 2027, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME Group. El banco central estadounidense subió el mes pasado su tasa de interés de referencia en un cuarto de punto porcentual, al rango del 3,75%-4,00%. El euro cayó un 0,41%, a 1,1152 dólares, alcanzando un mínimo de 17 meses frente al dólar y un piso 16 meses frente a la libra esterlina, ya que la subida de los precios del petróleo y las persistentes preocupaciones sobre la salud fiscal de Francia seguían lastrando a la moneda única. La libra esterlina bajó un 0,59%, a 1,3177 dólares. El yen japonés cedió un 0,08%, a 158,16 por dólar.

item.title: Televisa’s AT&T Mexico deal boosts its challenge to America Movil
item.description: Shares in Televisa rose on Wednesday after the Mexican broadcaster said it would buy AT&T's Mexican unit, in a move welcomed by investors that will set up a showdown with telecoms giant America Movil .
item.dc:creator: Paolo Laudani
item.content:encoded: Shares in Televisa (TLEVISACPO.MX) rose on Wednesday after the Mexican broadcaster said [USN:L4N45Z226 TEXT:"it would buy"] AT&T's Mexican unit, in a move welcomed by investors that will set up a showdown with telecoms giant America Movil (AMXB.MX) . The acquisition, if completed, would significantly expand Televisa’s telecom footprint, with Scotiabank analysts estimating its share of Mexico’s fixed and wireless subscribers would more than double to 19% from 8%. The increase in scale would strengthen Televisa’s position in a market dominated by America Movil, controlled by the family of Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim. However, analysts cautioned that integrating the new business and competing in Mexico’s costly, fiercely contested telecom sector could limit the benefits of the deal. Televisa could become a stronger rival, with more growth opportunities, by selling service bundles and earning more from its existing customers, analysts at UBS said. "We believe the transaction could be positive for the Mexican telecom industry. Consolidation usually leads to a greater focus on profitability, returns and cash generation," analysts at UBS said. The deal, worth $2 billion in cash and done in tandem with privately held Fintech Holdings, pushed shares up around 6% at 1944 GMT. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Investors aren't likely to expect major gains until the combined company delivers on expected results. EXECUTION RISKS The valuation represents a significant discount to comparable telecom companies in Latin America, but the acquisition carries some execution risks, Santander analysts wrote in a note. "Value will be created through turning around AT&T Mexico’s operations which have historically struggled (low margins) and eventually build out a convergent fixed-mobile offering ... which could also prove challenging," the note said. UBS also flagged execution as a challenge ahead for the new group. AT&T Mexico still requires network modernization and investment, particularly in 5G, and the deal's success will depend on THE management's ability to improve the network while generating cash, the bank said. Santander analysts expected little immediate effect on America Movil, citing its scale and dominant market position. Scotiabank, however, said the deal could intensify competitive pressure because the relatively low purchase price could allow Televisa and Fintech to devote more capital to network investment.

item.title: OpenAI employee who left for Apple took files about unreleased device, OpenAI alleges
item.description: An OpenAI employee who left the ChatGPT maker for Apple sent more than 100 files about an unreleased product to a personal account and later presented the product to senior Apple leadership, a new filing in the lawsuit between OpenAI and Apple alleges.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis, Deepa Seetharaman
item.content:encoded: An OpenAI employee who left the ChatGPT maker for Apple (AAPL.O) sent more than 100 files about an unreleased product to a personal account and later presented the product to senior Apple leadership, a new filing in the lawsuit between OpenAI and Apple alleges. In the filing in US federal court in San Jose, California, OpenAI alleged the presentation happened months ago and that Apple is now making AI products of its own, citing the release of Apple's [USN:L6N45Y122 TEXT:"HomeView product this week"]. "OpenAI is very concerned that its trade secret and confidential information is now circulating inside Apple, where Apple engineers can shape Apple’s upcoming products based on OpenAI’s confidential and innovative work," OpenAI said in its filing. Apple said it has policies and procedures in place to ensure new employees do not use confidential information from previous employers and it has found no evidence to support OpenAI's allegations. The document, filed on Tuesday, is part of an [USN:L4N43C1AC TEXT:"ongoing trade secret dispute"] filed by Apple earlier this year in which it alleged employees of the iPhone maker left and took confidential information to OpenAI's hardware division. OpenAI has denied those allegations. The dueling allegations underscore the intensifying battle between the two tech companies over talent and intellectual property as OpenAI pushes into consumer hardware, a market long dominated by Apple. In an October 12 letter to OpenAI, made public in another court filing on Wednesday, Apple's lawyers said the two personal phone numbers OpenAI identified as recipients of the files do not match the number the employee uses for his Apple work, so it appeared Apple did not have possession, custody or control of data sent to those numbers while he worked at OpenAI. Apple's lawyers also said there was no evidence so far of OpenAI files on Apple's servers based on Apple's investigation into repositories associated with his work. Apple had not learned of any presentation by the employee about unreleased OpenAI products and asked OpenAI for more information, the letter showed. In the court filing, Apple said OpenAI did not respond and instead went to court. Apple said it will continue to work with OpenAI to investigate the allegations. Earlier this week, US District Court Judge Edward Davila granted part of Apple's request to get early access to digital files from OpenAI in the suit. Davila said Apple could gather data from some of its former employees' devices and sit three of them for depositions on a sped-up schedule, including the two defendants in the case — Chang Liu, a former senior systems electrical engineer, and Tang Yew Tan, a former vice president of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch. The case is likely to go to trial in October 2027, though OpenAI has said in court filings that it could be ready for trial as soon as June 2027.

item.title: Bank of America consumer retail M&A banker Peacock to join JPMorgan, sources say
item.description: JPMorgan Chase is hiring senior consumer and retail M&A banker Richard Peacock from Bank of America , four people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Svea Herbst-Bayliss, Abigail Summerville
item.content:encoded: JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) is hiring senior consumer and retail M&A banker Richard Peacock from Bank of America (BAC.N) , four people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday. Peacock, who joined Bank of America over a decade ago, will take the role of global head of consumer and retail M&A at JPMorgan early next year and be based in New York, said the people, who work in the financial industry and were not authorized to speak about his move publicly. He is the [USN:L1N45Z0KM TEXT:"latest in a string"] of managing directors to leave Bank of America, the United States' second-largest bank, at a time the hot M&A market is prompting other personnel moves on Wall Street. Earlier this year, Peacock was named co-head of Bank of America's newly created private capital M&A group to help private equity firms across sectors monetize their assets. Bank of America and JPMorgan declined to comment. Peacock could not be reached for comment. Earlier this month, JPMorgan said it hired former Sycamore Partners [USN:L4N45S14L TEXT:"executive Rob Sweeney"] as global chair of investment banking. He will advise major corporate clients, particularly in the consumer and retail sector, and work with senior bankers on key relationships. The bank also hired Ian Carnegie-Brown, who is based in London, from UBS this year. JPMorgan's consumer and retail investment banking team ranked No. 1 in the Dealogic industry rankings in the first six months of 2026 and for all of 2025. The bank served as financial adviser when Alimentation Couche-Tard announced plans to buy convenience store chain Zabka and when food ingredients maker Ingredion agreed to acquire rival Tate & Lyle. Bank of America lost another senior consumer and retail dealmaker over the summer when Andrew Conway [USN:L6N42H0XY TEXT:"departed"] to become Citigroup's (C.N) global chair of consumer and retail investment banking. JPMorgan has hired several prominent Bank of America bankers in recent months, including David Fishman, Amy Lissauer and Kevin Brunner. But Bank of America has said it continues to invest in talent and has hired more than 40 new managing directors in the corporate and investment bank this year.

item.title: Banks, buildings burn as Albania's capital Tirana erupts into student violence
item.description: Tens of thousands of students stormed the streets of Tirana on Wednesday, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and corruption.
item.dc:creator: Fatos Bytyci
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of students stormed the streets of Tirana on Wednesday, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and corruption. Police responded with water cannons and tear gas to disperse protesters who started a fire at the ministry of education building, overturned garbage cans and smashed the fronts of local businesses, Reuters footage showed. A Raiffeisen Bank branch near the education ministry also caught fire, a Reuters witness said. The protests represent the most violent outburst against Prime Minister Edi Rama, who won a fourth term in office in elections in May last year but has since faced growing discontent at [USN:L6N3ZC0BA TEXT:"perceived graft"] surrounding top officials. Protesters also dismiss opposition figures as unpalatable alternatives. The unrest caps a summer of peaceful protests against Rama, triggered by the proposed development of a [USN:L6N4380FB TEXT:"luxury resort"] along Albania's pristine southern coast backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner which has been [USN:L6N42J18T TEXT:"caught up in legal disputes"]. "This is a revolution. We are tired of peaceful protests. We will not stop until Rama resigns," said Lora, a student who declined to give her last name said as she threw rocks at the police. Others chanted "Resignation" and "Police of crime." WIDER PROTESTS Student organisers said the protest was over conditions at universities, higher education costs, a lack of financial support and employment prospects after graduation. The unrest is part of a broader wave of student activism sweeping Europe over education and living conditions. In France, high school students have staged [USN:L1N45U08J TEXT:"weeks of protests"] and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education. Albanian media reported that Wednesday's protests spread to universities at Elbasan and Shkodra. The government condemned the violence. "Protesting is a legitimate right, but it cannot be used as an excuse for violence, city destruction or ugly fighting in the middle of the road," Deputy Prime Minister Albana Kociu said on Facebook. "I call on students and every honest citizen who believes in the right to protest: Distance yourself from violence and vandalism!" The police issued a statement calling for calm. "Any person who uses violence, burns or destroys property, or attacks Police officers, bears individual responsibility and will face the law, in accordance with the offences committed," it said.

item.title: Mexico to require digital platforms to shield minors from harmful content
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she will sign a presidential decree on Wednesday requiring digital platforms, including social media and streaming sites, to shield children and teenagers from violent, sexual and other harmful content.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she will sign a presidential decree on Wednesday requiring digital platforms, including social media and streaming sites, to shield children and teenagers from violent, sexual and other harmful content. The decree, which will step up scrutiny of big technology companies in Latin America's second-largest economy, comes after an [USN:L6N45N12T TEXT:"attack by two 18-year-old former students on a high school"] in the northern state of Coahuila in early October left one person dead and wounded three others. Digital platforms will have one month to come into compliance with the decree, government adviser Luisa Maria Alcalde said. Sheinbaum added that if companies failed to follow the decree, the government would back a bill to penalize the platforms. Officials said they had already met with representatives of Meta (META.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Apple (AAPL.O) , TikTok, Google (GOOGL.O) , X and Huawei to discuss the matter. A Meta spokesperson told Reuters that the company, which runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads, is "aware of the decree" and that it will "analyze it in detail," adding that it has long had tools in place to help parents "guide their children's digital experience.” "We will continue to engage with the authorities to help create a safer digital environment for teenagers in the country,” the spokesperson said, adding that Meta offers safety features on its platforms which include safeguards to limit who can make contact with children, as well as the monitoring of viewed content. Microsoft, Apple, TikTok, Google, X and Huawei did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. Mexico's move follows a broader [USN:L8N42Q0MC TEXT:"global push"] to protect minors online, with governments in Europe and Australia tightening oversight of digital platforms and US states pursuing a range of child-safety measures. [USN:S0N3S10A3 TEXT:"Brazil"] has also moved to strengthen protections for children online. Such measures have raised questions over how to protect minors while safeguarding privacy and freedom of expression.

item.title: Mukesh Ambani's Jio seeks $108 billion valuation in record Indian IPO
item.description: Jio Platforms is set to raise up to $3.2 billion in India's largest IPO to date, which will value the group founded by billionaire Mukesh Ambani at as much as $108.3 billion.
item.dc:creator: Vivek M, Vibhuti Sharma
item.content:encoded: Jio Platforms is set to raise up to $3.2 billion in India's largest IPO to date, which will value the group founded by billionaire Mukesh Ambani at as much as $108.3 billion. The telecoms, cloud and AI group, which counts Meta (META.O) and Google among its major overseas investors, said on Wednesday it will open its IPO on October 21 and close it on October 23. Jio has set a price band of 1,065 to 1,119 rupees per share and bidding for anchor investors will take place on October 19. It will offer 270 million new shares in the IPO. Launched in 2016, Jio upended India's telecoms sector by offering free voice and data plans that allowed many Indians to access services such as YouTube and Facebook for the first time. Competitors including Bharti Airtel (BRTI.NS) and Vodafone Idea (VODA.NS) were hit hard and Reliance Jio Infocomm is now the biggest player in the sector with 533 million subscribers and a 60% share of India's data traffic. Jio cautioned in its updated prospectus that India's data-protection and telecom rules may limit data-driven monetisation, a risk for a company whose growth pitch leans on turning its vast user base into advertising and digital-services revenue. In 2020, Jio raised more than $20.5 billion from 13 global investors in exchange for an equity stake of around 33%, valuing it at between $57 billion and $65 billion at the time. SET TO RANK AMONG BIGGEST INDIAN COMPANIES At a valuation of $108.3 billion, Jio Platforms would rank as India's fourth-biggest company by market capitalisation, behind parent Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel and India's largest private lender HDFC Bank (HDBK.NS) . Jio plans to use up to 275 billion Indian rupees ($2.89 billion) of the proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings at its telecoms unit which is run by Mukesh Ambani's son Akash. The rest will be used for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditure. The IPO follows the listing of [USN:L4N45G0A8 TEXT:"National Stock Exchange of India"] (NSEI.BO) in September which raised $2.3 billion, underscoring investor appetite for large offerings in India. India's largest share offering so far was by Hyundai Motor India (HYUN.NS) which raised $2.9 billion in 2024. ($1 = 95.1500 Indian rupees)

item.title: US inflation heats up in September; Fed rate hike this month back on table
item.description: US consumer prices accelerated in September as the cost of gasoline surged, dealing another blow to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party ahead of the November 3 midterm elections and putting an interest rate increase later this month back on the radar.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: US consumer prices accelerated in September as the cost of gasoline surged, dealing another blow to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party ahead of the November 3 midterm elections and putting an interest rate increase later this month back on the radar. The Consumer Price Index report from the Labor Department on Wednesday showed a broadening of price pressures beyond energy, raising concerns among economists that underlying inflation could be getting sticky. There was also an AI-related boost to inflation last month. Financial markets now see the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision at its October 27-28 meeting as a closer call than before the data was released. The report added to surveys this month that showed a further deterioration in [USN:L1N45V0J1 TEXT:"consumer sentiment"] and a plunge in Trump's [USN:L6N45D0XN TEXT:"approval rating"], driven by angst over the rising cost of living. A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed about 78% of Americans [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"blamed Trump's"] policies, including tariffs and the Middle East conflict, for rising prices, which are outpacing wages. "The inflation we're experiencing right now is largely the result of erratic policy from the executive branch," said Kyle Moore, chief economist at the Century Foundation, a progressive think tank. "Worse still, the directionless war in Iran continues to disrupt global supply chains. This administration has also been wholly unwilling to moderate the pace of the AI and data-center buildout." The CPI rose 0.6% last month after climbing 0.4% in August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said, in line with economists' expectations. In the 12 months through September, the CPI advanced 3.7% after rising 3.4% in August. A 9.1% surge in gasoline prices accounted for more than half of the increase in the CPI over the month. The US-Israeli war with Iran is driving up [USN:L1N46003I TEXT:"energy prices"]. Other motor fuels, which include diesel, soared 11.9% last month and were up 60.9% on a year-over-year basis. Diesel prices at the pump are at record highs, and there are fears that those costs will soon feed through to higher prices at the supermarket. Food prices were unchanged after gaining 0.1% in both July and August. Grocery store prices dipped 0.1% over the month as beef prices dropped 1.0% and the cost of dairy and related products eased 0.9%. Egg prices declined 1.3%. But prices for nonalcoholic beverages surged 0.9%, while fruits and vegetables cost 0.5% more, with banana prices shooting up 1.0%, in what could be early signs of rising trucking costs being passed on to consumers. Lettuce prices rebounded 3.9% as a cyclospora outbreak faded. Grocery prices rose 1.8% on a year-over-year basis. Average hourly earnings for all employees declined 0.7% in September from a year ago, after falling 0.3% in August, underscoring the squeeze on consumers in what economists call the bottom of a K-shaped economy. Economists said this data raised doubts about whether consumers could maintain their robust pace of spending. "While much of the lost purchasing power is due to rising energy costs, there is no reason to expect that to fade in the near term," said Eric Winograd, chief US economist at AllianceBernstein. "The bottom part of the K-shaped economy is losing ground, as anybody who has seen campaign ads on TV the last few weeks has heard." With the cost of living rising, the Social Security Administration announced a [USN:L1N45Z0SL TEXT:"3.6% cost-of-living adjustment"] for Social Security and Supplemental Security Income benefits for 2027. The programs benefit nearly 72 million Americans, including retirees, the disabled and certain widows, widowers and children. Social Security retirement benefits will, on average, increase by $75 per month. Stocks on Wall Street fell. The dollar advanced versus a basket of currencies. Yields on US Treasury notes and bonds rose. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI rose 0.3% in September, matching the gain in August. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the so-called core CPI would increase 0.2%. The core CPI was lifted by a 0.4% advance in the cost of shelter, including hotel and motel rooms. Owners' equivalent rent, a measure of the amount homeowners would pay to rent or would earn from renting their property, rose 0.3%. Airline fares rose 1.2% amid higher jet fuel prices. Consumers paid more for gardening and lawn care services, likely reflecting worker shortages amid a crackdown on undocumented immigrants. The costs of recreation and education also rose, as did those of hospital and dental services. Overall services prices increased 0.4%. They were also up 0.4% excluding energy. Core goods prices rose 0.3%, pushed up by a 0.7% increase in the cost of used cars and trucks. Apparel prices climbed 0.3% and the cost of toys rebounded 4.2%, suggesting some lingering pass-through from tariffs. But prescription medication was cheaper. Prices for computers and peripherals jumped 1.3%, reflecting AI-related investment, while the cost of computer software and accessories rebounded 0.4%. In the 12 months through September, core CPI inflation was 2.6%, compared with 2.4% in August. The US central bank tracks the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index for its 2% inflation target. Financial markets raised the chances of a rate hike at the Fed's meeting this month to roughly 37% from about 22% prior to the release of the CPI report, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. The odds of a rate increase this month had diminished following [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"underwhelming payroll"] gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected PCE [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"inflation readings"] for July and August. The Fed in September raised its [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"overnight benchmark interest rate"] by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range, its first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the months ahead. Most economists continue to expect the Fed will hold rates steady this month and raise them in December. Based on the CPI data, economists' estimates for core PCE inflation ranged from 0.3% to 0.4%, which would mean a year-over-year reading of 3.1%. Producer price data being released on Thursday could impact those estimates. Core PCE inflation was 0.2% in August and 3.0% on a year-over-year basis. "What is interesting is that the primary drivers of inflation are supply-side policies that are better addressed by the fiscal authority," said Joseph Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM. "However, that is not going to happen anytime soon, which leaves the Fed to address a re-establishment of price stability."

item.title: Ukraine says SpaceX hampers drones for attack and defence, as US ties fray
item.description: Ukraine said Elon Musk’s SpaceX had restricted Starlink services on Wednesday, hampering the country's attack and air-defence drone missions as worsening ties with Washington fuel concerns over US battlefield support.
item.dc:creator: Yuliia Dysa, Dan Peleschuk
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said Elon Musk’s SpaceX had restricted Starlink services on Wednesday, hampering the country's attack and air-defence drone missions as worsening ties with Washington fuel concerns over US battlefield support. Russia launched more missiles and drones at Ukrainian cities, knocking out power to hundreds of thousands in attacks that President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called “ostentatious disrespect” for US President Donald Trump’s call for an energy ceasefire. Trump turned on Zelenskiy after lifting sanctions on Russian diesel to ease pressure on fuel prices that have soared since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February. He told Kyiv to stop attacking Russian refineries and urged Ukrainians to replace Zelenskiy. "It's painful when President Trump chooses one side, not our side," Zelenskiy told "Piers Morgan Uncensored". He said he was OK with Trump being in the middle of Ukraine and Russia, but "if you are in the middle, you have to stay in the middle." Asked about the restriction on the military version of SpaceX's Starlink services in Ukraine, Zelenskiy said: "It's a big mistake ... This decision will bring a lot of human losses." He did not say who was responsible. Musk, the CEO of SpaceX, which operates Starlink, said the US government controlled the system's speeds. "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Musk wrote on the social media platform X, using the acronym for president of the United States. Musk is a close political ally of Trump's. In the interview, Zelenskiy also dismissed Trump's comment that Ukraine [USN:S0N43U01D TEXT:"needed a new leader"]. "It is a decision of our people," Zelenskiy said. "No Trump, no Musk, not anyone in the world can choose the president or elect in other countries." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The developments come as Trump's Republican allies [USN:L1N45V0SB TEXT:"face mounting pressure"] over the cost of living ahead of November's midterm elections, with [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"fuel prices and household expenses"] weighing on voters and prompting the administration to seek ways to ease energy costs. Sources have told Reuters and other media that the US has threatened to cut off intelligence for early warning of missile strikes on Ukraine, to press Kyiv to suspend attacks on Russian oil refineries. Ukrainian officials said late on Tuesday they had received no warnings from Western partners for a second day before Russian missiles hit the capital. Trump said on Tuesday that Washington was still sharing intelligence. In comments posted on Telegram after [USN:L8N45Z21K TEXT:"talks in London"] with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Zelenskiy said: "It is clear that the Russians are trying to take advantage of the problems with Starlink in Ukraine as the operation of interceptor drones largely depends on that connection." Burnham announced the planned delivery of £45 million ($59.6 million) of surface-to-air missiles used to target jet-powered Russian drones, with £10 million of that package fast-tracked to meet an urgent need in Ukraine. Trump said at the weekend that Ukraine and Russia both agreed to halt attacks on energy targets, although neither side confirmed this and intensive Russian bombing over the last two days included Ukrainian power stations. After a night of bombardment of the capital Kyiv, Russian strikes continued throughout the day on Wednesday with six people killed in the western city of Lutsk, where the regional governor said a warehouse and a residential building were hit. Ukraine, for its part, continued long-range strikes on Russia, hitting Russia's biggest [USN:L8N46009S TEXT:"data centre"], although it says it is holding back from hitting energy targets for now to show respect for Trump. NO WARNING BEFORE STARLINK CUTS Ukrainian military officials said Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) had without warning started to interrupt functioning of its military-grade terminals when they were moving at high speed. Kyiv installs SpaceX receptors in many of its drones as part of their onboard guidance systems. The terminals operate across Ukraine, including in territory held by Russian forces. "Our defence forces did not receive a warning about this limitation, and this led to the disruption of several missions," presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram, saying the restriction affected Starshield, SpaceX's military and intelligence service. The speed cutoff hampers Ukraine's ability to conduct strikes on Russian targets inside Ukraine, and also to defend itself from Russian drones using its own interceptor drones, according to a Defence Ministry source and another military source. Beskrestnov said SpaceX had imposed a speed limit of 160 kph (100 mph). The Defence Ministry source told Reuters military units had reported guidance systems losing their connections at speeds of less than half that. The Defence Ministry source said Ukraine was in contact with the company, the US government and NATO to seek clarification over the sudden limitations. The suggestion that Musk's company had limited Ukrainian military capabilities drew a sharp response from Poland, which pays for Ukrainian Starlink subscriptions on Kyiv's behalf. "Hey, @elonmusk, big man, are you playing politics with your products again?" Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski asked Musk on X. "As your European customers, we are watching you." There was no immediate response from Musk, who in the past has called Sikorski a "small man." NO WARNING AHEAD OF MISSILES Rescue workers in Kyiv were stretchering the injured from the wreckage of a blasted-out residential building overnight, while firefighters battled a huge blaze in the darkness. Officials said 2 people were killed and 21 wounded at the site. Some 600,000 people were left without power as Russian missiles struck power stations during hours of attacks that primarily targeted Kyiv and Kharkiv, Ukraine's two biggest cities. Russia's Defence Ministry confirmed it had struck four power plants in and around Kyiv and two in Kharkiv, among other targets. Zelenskiy said 30 energy facilities were damaged. Zelenskiy cast the latest Russian attacks as a deliberate snub to Trump's declaration of a ceasefire on energy targets. "Russia does not consider the American President's statements strong," Zelenskiy wrote on X. "The strike was entirely deliberate and demonstrative in its scale – Russia has never before shown such ostentatious disrespect toward the United States."

item.title: TSX falls as miners take a hit, hot US inflation weighs
item.description: Canada's main stock index closed in the red on Wednesday, as weaker metal prices weighed on miners, while hot US inflation data increased odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike later this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index closed in the red on Wednesday, as weaker metal prices weighed on miners, while hot US inflation data increased odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike later this month. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) closed down 1.11%, at 35,584.46, falling from a three-week peak. US [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer prices"] accelerated in September on higher gasoline costs, boosting expectations for a rate hike later this month. Increased bets that the Fed will hike rates further to tame inflation also weighed on [USN:L6N4601AB TEXT:"US indexes"]. In Canada, the materials sector (.GSPTTMT) was the biggest drag on the index, declining 4.3% as precious metal prices fell further after the data. The rate-sensitive financial sector (.SPTTFS) , which includes heavyweight banks, also fell 0.5%. Technology shares (.SPTTTK) fell 2.4% with Celestica (CLS.TO) down 9.2% and Shopify (SHOP.TO) falling 2.2% . "Canada will join other global central banks in hiking interest rates, but I don't think they're going to deliver as much as futures or the bond market is currently expecting," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones The energy sector (.SPTTEN) gained just 0.07%, as oil prices held firm over $100 per barrel Reuters reported that Iran was using new tactics to target ships, seeking to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections Yields on the Canadian benchmark 10-year bond rose to 3.872%. Canada is [USN:L4N4600EH TEXT:"pursuing "]a trade pact with India and closer EU ties to reduce reliance on the US, ahead of Indian PM Narendra Modi's visit in [USN:S0N44S00M TEXT:"December"] Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings (FFH.TO) will buy a [USN:L1N4600FH TEXT:"majority"] stake in India's IDBI Bank (IDBI.NS) in a deal worth 528.78 billion Indian rupees ($5.56 billion), the Indian government said. Fairfax shares were flat.

item.title: Ohio's working-class voters rethink support for Trump and the Republican Party
item.description: The stakes are high in Ohio, where Republicans are defending a US Senate seat and the governor's office.
item.dc:creator: Richard Cowan
item.content:encoded: A decade after Republican Donald Trump peeled away working-class and union voters who had long been a cornerstone of Democratic support in Ohio, Democrats and labor leaders see an opening to win back some of them in the November 3 US elections . Now midway through his second term, the president's magic appears to be losing at least some of its luster with blue-collar men and women as rising prices, the Iran war and concerns about his rhetoric prompt some voters to reconsider their support. The state's reputation as a leading swing state began to fade in 2016 when Trump won strong support from working-class voters who felt their economic concerns were being heard, helping turn Ohio into a reliably Republican state. Almost overnight, Ohio became rock-solid Republican. Ohio voted for the eventual winner in 14 straight presidential elections from 1964 until 2020 when Democrat Joe Biden won nationally but Ohio backed Trump. A shift in Ohio toward Democrats could matter in elections that will help determine whether Republicans retain control of Congress during Trump's final two years in office or hand new leverage [USN:L6N45U0XV TEXT:"to Democrats"] over his agenda. The stakes are high in Ohio, where Republicans are defending a US Senate seat and the governor's office. Two House races are rated [USN:L1N45R0LS TEXT:""toss-ups.""] One, in northwestern Ohio, has long been held by a Democrat and the other, in northeastern Ohio, is Republican-held. Trump is not on the ballot this time but has told supporters to act as if he is. It remains to be seen whether that could end up helping or hindering Republicans running in tough races. Republican Senator Jon Husted is in a tight competition with Democratic former Senator Sherrod Brown, while Democrat Amy Acton is challenging Republican Vivek Ramaswamy for an open governor's seat. Trump campaigned with Husted and Ramaswamy in Youngstown on Monday to try to energize the Republican base.
